title: War-damaged Gaza building collapses, killing at least 20 people
summary: Health officials in Gaza say a building damaged months ago by an Israeli strike has collapsed, killing people from 6 displaced families who had taken shelter inside.
story: A building housing displaced Palestinian families collapsed in Gaza City on Wednesday, killing at least 20 people, most of them women and children, according to local health officials. The multistory structure was heavily damaged during the Israel-Hamas war and there had been warnings about its safety.

The building was housing about six displaced families when it collapsed on Wednesday morning. At least 15 others were injured, and the 20 dead included eight children and six women, according to the Gaza Civil Defense rescue agency. The toll was expected to rise as more bodies were recovered from the debris.
Video showed civil defense crews surveying the wreckage and using bulldozers to dig people out, including children.

The building had been partially destroyed in an Israeli strike early in the war between Israel and Hamas. It was not immediately clear what caused the collapse, but in Gaza — where the majority of buildings have been damaged or destroyed — dozens of bombed-out, multistory structures have collapsed throughout the war, particularly during winter weather.
Building collapses have become a major hazard in Gaza. Displaced families have often returned from tent camps to homes damaged by bombardment during the almost three years of war.
Gaza war still simmering despite U.S.-brokered ceasefire
While the heaviest fighting in Gaza has subsided since a fragile U.S.-brokered ceasefire took hold in October
last year, Israel has continued to carry out strikes in the decimated Palestinian territory, including some Monday and Tuesday that killed several people.

The violence has continued despite a visit last month by Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law and a key Mideast negotiator, who met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an effort to push the ceasefire deal forward.

Speaking a couple weeks after his visit to the region, Kushner directly linked the lack of progress on the rehabilitation of Gaza to Israeli elections set to take place in late October. Polls show it is a tight race between Netanyahu and his opponents.

"We're working through some political issues in Israel. I think we agree with them on the end state," Kushner said. "They just have a crazy election, and that makes them a little irrational in certain regards."
Militants have carried out shooting attacks on Israeli troops, and Israel says its strikes are in response to those and other ceasefire violations.

The Gaza war was sparked by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel in 2023, which killed around 1,200 people and saw 251 others taken hostage. Israel's retaliatory offensive in Gaza has killed more than 73,264 Palestinians, including those killed since the ceasefire, according to the Gaza Health Ministry.

title: Photos show widespread damage at U.S. positions caused by Iranian attacks
summary: The images were sent to CBS News by active service members under condition of anonymity.
story: New photos obtained exclusively by CBS News reveal for the first time the widespread damage and destruction of buildings and vehicles at multiple U.S. positions across the Middle East, as a result of Iranian missile and drone attacks.
The images were sent to CBS News by active service members on condition of anonymity because of rigid media restrictions within the military.

"This is major damage to our bases that hasn't been communicated to the American public," one deployed service member told CBS News. "We're standing there with our eyes closed getting punched in the face."

One photo, taken at Prince Sultan Air Force Base in Saudi Arabia, shows a direct hit on the back half of a Boeing E-3 Sentry four-engine aircraft, its tail severed from the charred fuselage that also supported a rotating radar that is essential for collecting midair intelligence.

Other photos taken from the base show hollowed-out buildings and barracks whose shells ironically stand next to unaffected cement "T-wall" structures, which were once regarded as critical fortifications against grenade and mortar attacks but proved critically ineffective against an aerial assault.

Similarly grim pictures were captured at Camp Buehring in Kuwait, a major staging area for U.S. Army ground troops, armored vehicles and some aircraft; the post is located in a remote desert region far northwest of Kuwait City.

The Defense Department's inspector general this week released a fresh report on the war in Iran that revealed "equipment losses" worth up to $3.7 billion — including nearly 60 aircraft. In a first-of-its-kind mandatory report to Congress, the inspector general added that U.S. Central Command reported Iranian strikes at U.S. bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman and Jordan.
The Pentagon did not respond to a request for comment.

"These are not 'squirters' getting through," the service member added, referencing language used by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after the deadly March 1 attack on Port of Shuaiba in Kuwait that killed six U.S. troops. "We're not defending these bases. We're just watching them get destroyed."

title: 'Double Lives' star says being kicked out of church over adult content career didn't shake her faith
summary: Tammy from "Double Lives of Suburban Wives" reveals being kicked out of her church over adult content creation and how she chose forgiveness.
story: ‘Double Lives of Suburban Wives’ star Tammy discusses being kicked out of her church, maintaining her faith in God and challenging critics to recognize that everyone is imperfec

title: 'American Idol' ditches Hollywood for Georgia after two decades as California loses another production
summary: "American Idol" is relocating from Hollywood to an Atlanta-area studio complex as Georgia's tax incentives and infrastructure lure major productions.
story: California gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton joins ‘America’s Newsroom’ to discuss President Donald Trump’s push for a federal film tax credit to bring entertainment jobs back to California. He also weighs in on a new state tire regulation and a Los Angeles crosswalk controversy.
"American Idol" is ditching Hollywood for Georgia amid renewed concerns about California’s competitiveness.

On Wednesday, Fremantle, the production company behind ABC's long-running singing competition, confirmed the relocation to Fox News Digital. The company is reportedly in final discussions with an Atlanta-area studio complex, according to Deadline.
Longtime fans and viewers of the show were quick to react on social media.
"'You’re going to…Atlanta!' Just doesn’t have that same ring to it," one user wrote on X.
"Another one bites the dust LA. Sad!" another added.
"So much for those 'hollyweird' tax breaks eh?" one person quipped.
NEWSOM SAYS FILM TAX INCENTIVES ARE BRINGING HOLLYWOOD HOME BUT INDUSTRY EXPERTS WARN IT MAY BE 'TOO LATE'
Lionel Richie, Carrie Underwood, Ryan Seacrest and Luke Bryan will be filming the 27th season of "American Idol" in Georgia. (Disney via Getty Images)
"LOL !!! Another production Hollywood GETTING THE HELL OUT OF CALIFORNIA ! AFTER 25 YEARS BYEEEEE GAVIN NEWSOM American Idol is OUT OF CALI," another wrote.

While the move marks a significant change for a series long associated with Hollywood, Lisa Cusack, president of the Don’t L.A. My Burbank PAC, said the relocation should be a warning to California officials.

"The issue is that Georgia offers generous incentives for reality TV shows, while California often leaves them behind," Cusack told Fox News Digital. "For example, Nick Schultz’s entertainment tax credit bill, AB 2319, specifically excludes unscripted programming."

"Now Georgia has a lot of the same infrastructure as Hollywood, and offers a less expensive, more family-friendly quality of life," she continued. "There’s very little keeping even Hollywood business in California anymore. This should serve as a five-shot-espresso wake-up call to Rob Bonta to settle with Paramount and not make things worse."

Last month, Paramount CEO David Ellison threatened to relocate the company’s headquarters to a more business-friendly state such as Georgia, Tennessee or Texas if California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who is leading 11 other states in an effort to block Paramount's $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), did not negotiate a settlement by Oct. 1.
PARAMOUNT-WARNER BROS DISCOVERY ANTITRUST TRIAL DATE SET; MERGER PUT ON PAUSE OVER LEGAL BATTLE
The next season of "Idol" will premiere next year. (Eric McCandless/Disney via Getty Images)

Puck News first reported Ellison's potential exit plans.

As Puck News reported, Ellison could move Paramount — and potentially Warner Bros. Discovery if he ultimately merges the companies — out of California "regardless of the eventual outcome of the case." Ellison has even developed a five-year plan that would relocate the vast majority of jobs out of the state while still maintaining a footprint in Hollywood.

On Wednesday, TMZ reported that the Los Angeles Mayor's Office and the California Attorney General's Office were told Paramount would announce Tuesday that it was leaving California. No such announcement had been made as of Wednesday.

"I tried to warn you," Spencer Pratt wrote on X following the TMZ news. "LA is getting absolutely decimated by the insane communist wackos running California. Bob Bonta’s jihad against Paramount is a death blow. What a corrupt piece of s---."

According to Deadline, Georgia has become one of the country’s most competitive production hubs by offering a 20% base film and television tax credit, with a potential 10% promotional uplift for qualifying projects. The state’s official guidelines list television series among eligible productions and require at least $500,000 in qualified Georgia spending.
Stephen Weizenecker, a partner at Barnes & Thornburg in Georgia, said there are three pillars to analyze when deciding whether to film in California or Georgia.

"Physical infrastructure is equally critical. A show like 'American Idol' requires massive sound stages, specialized equipment for elaborate performance sets, live-audience capacity, and proximity to rehearsal spaces, wardrobe, and production offices," said Weizenecker, who has had a direct role in developing Georgia's entertainment tax incentive framework and spent over two decades advising productions on filming all across the world.
"Idol" judge Carrie Underwood is one of many celebrities who has fled Los Angeles. (Christopher Willard/Disney via Getty Images)

"Georgia now offers purpose-built studio campuses — including Tyler Perry Studios, Trilith Studios and Assembly Studios — that rival Los Angeles market in scale and amenities. I have worked closely with many of these facilities as they grew from concept to world-class campuses, and I can attest to their capacity to support the most demanding productions."
Weizenecker said production tax incentives often serve as the "decisive tipping point" once the infrastructure boxes are checked.
CARRIE UNDERWOOD SAYS HER FAMILY COULD BE 'SELF-SUSTAINED' ON TENNESSEE FARM AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD SPOTLIGHT

"As someone instrumental in crafting the Georgia Entertainment Industry Investment Act, I have seen firsthand how Georgia's program offers structural advantages over California's that make it exceptionally attractive for a recurring, high-budget unscripted series."
Additionally, Georgia has invested strategically in workforce development since the enactment of the Georgia Entertainment Industry Investment Act, according to Weizenecker.

"The Georgia Film Academy, a collaboration among the University System of Georgia, the Technical College System of Georgia and the Georgia Department of Economic Development, has trained thousands of professionals across disciplines from grip and electric to visual effects. That pipeline, reinforced by the sheer volume of annual production activity, has created a self-sustaining ecosystem of IATSE-qualified crew members who live and work in the state full-time."

Last month, Paramount CEO David Ellison threatened to relocate the company’s headquarters to a more business-friendly state such as Georgia, Tennessee or Texas if California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who is leading 11 other states in an effort to block Paramount's $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), did not negotiate a settlement by Oct. 1. (Michael Yanow/NurPhoto via Getty Images; Justin Sullivan/Getty Images)

"Virtually every major production services vendor — equipment rental, transportation, catering, construction and specialty providers — now maintains a permanent Georgia presence," he continued. "Post-production facilities offering editorial, color grading, sound mixing and VFX have expanded significantly, with several national and international post houses establishing Atlanta-area operations."

"The same infrastructure supporting Marvel, Lucasfilm, Netflix and major network television productions is available to a show of 'American Idol's' caliber," he added. "Having advised many of the productions and facilities that anchor this ecosystem, I can confirm Georgia's vendor community is fully capable of supporting this show."
The show’s relocation also underscores how its talent is already less tied to Los Angeles.
Carrie Underwood, who won "American Idol" in 2005 and now serves as one of the show’s judges, has lived with her family on a 400-acre farm in Franklin, Tennessee, since leaving Hollywood in 2019.
Carrie Underwood says she and her family are "self-sustained" on their Tennessee farm. (Carrie Underwood Instagram)
Underwood has described her Tennessee home as the place where she and her husband, former NHL player Mike Fisher, raise their two sons, care for livestock and grow vegetables.
In a recent interview with Fox News Digital, Underwood said farm life is the opposite of her on-camera career and that she takes pride in being a hands-on mother when she is home.

title: Macklemore donates $1M to Palestinian aid organizations after Ed Sheeran tour fallout
summary: Macklemore is donating $1 million from Ed Sheeran's U.S. "Loop Tour" to Palestinian aid groups and challenged Robert Kraft to match his contribution.
story: Rapper Macklemore causes chaos on Ed Sheerans tour after making anti-Israel comments at a concert. Ed Sheeran responds to the backlash, explaining that the decision to remove Macklemore was made by promoters.

Macklemore announced that he is donating the $1 million he earned opening for Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour to organizations providing humanitarian aid to Palestinians, prompting a public response from New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft.

On Monday, the 43-year-old rapper was dropped from Sheeran's "Loop Tour" after he repeatedly called for a "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" during his opening act at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sept. 4 and 5.

Macklemore alleged that Kraft, 85, pressured Sheeran to remove him from the tour by telling the singer he would not be allowed to perform at Gillette Stadium and by rallying other stadium owners to issue a similar ultimatum. Kraft later confirmed he opposed Macklemore's participation at Gillette based on what he described as the "Thrift Shop" rapper's history of antisemitic rhetoric.
ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO
Sheeran, 35, has said the decision was made by the tour promoter and venue owners, not by him personally.

In an Instagram post on Wednesday, Macklemore shared his plans to donate his paycheck from the "Loop Tour" to six organizations, including the Palestine Children's Relief Fund (PCRF), HEAL Palestine, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians, UNRWA USA National Committee and American Near East Refugee Aid (ANERA).

"With everything that has happened over the last 48 hours, I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation, and still fighting for their freedom," he wrote.
Macklemore announced that he is donating $1 million in earnings from Ed Sheeran's tour after he was dropped. (Redferns)

"I will be donating the entire $1 million of my net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour to six organizations working directly to support the Palestinian people," he continued. "And I invite Robert Kraft to match my donation. Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protecting. A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any other life on this earth."

"I want to center the parents carrying their children into hospitals without the basic resources to treat them, and the physicians, paramedics, journalists and aid workers who keep going back in. I want to center the organizers and activists who have paid real costs for standing with Palestine," Macklemore added. "Their risk is of a far different order than mine."
HANNAH EINBINDER'S BRUTAL MESSAGE TO ED SHEERAN FUELS GROWING CELEBRITY REVOLT OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR DRAMA
Macklemore noted that "writing a check is one of the least costly forms of solidarity to me."
"I am doing it because I can and because these organizations are doing the work while much of the world debates it," he wrote.

"Palestinians have lived for decades without basic rights and should not have to wait another day to be free," Macklemore added. "That is where my focus will remain. I will continue to stand with the Palestinian people and their fight for liberation."
MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE
"When the news cycle moves on, which it will, don’t move with it," he concluded. "Free Palestine."

Shortly after the rapper challenged Kraft to match his contribution, Kraft said Sheeran had already asked him to commit $2 million to match the singer's own donation toward humanitarian relief in the region.
New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft said Sheeran asked to match his $2M contribution to humanitarian aid in the region. (Ron Chenoy/Imagn Images)

"I have dedicated much of my life to building bridges between all people. I believe deeply that all lives are worth protecting. Earlier today, before Macklemore challenged me to match his donation, Ed called me and asked me to commit $2 million to match his donation to aid in the region and fight this humanitarian crisis," Kraft wrote in a statement shared on Gillette Stadium's social media pages.
MACKLEMORE'S LONG HISTORY OF CONTROVERSY FROM GRAMMY WINS TO 'FREE PALESTINE' CONCERT REMARKS
"Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges," Kraft continued.

"In addition, I’d like the people who are speaking in support of the Palestinian people to know that for decades, I have supported efforts that create opportunity for Palestinians and have brought young Palestinians and Israelis together to build businesses, create jobs, and forge relationships," he added.

title: Kelly Osbourne draws a line with estranged sister Aimee: 'I don't want you in my life'

Kelly Osbourne reflected on the lost relationship with her estranged older sister, Aimee Osbourne.

The youngest daughter of late rock legend Ozzy Osbourne admitted on an episode of the "We Need To Talk" podcast that she's not close with her sister, but that she did "respect her enough to, you know, keep her anonymity."

"I believe there's a reason for everything; it just wasn't meant to be for her," she explained of Aimee's decision against participating in the family's wildly successful reality show, "The Osbournes."

title: Hannah Einbinder's brutal message to Ed Sheeran fuels growing celebrity revolt over Macklemore tour drama
summary: Hannah Einbinder roasted Ed Sheeran on Instagram after Macklemore was dropped from the "Loop Tour" over his onstage pro-Palestinian comments.
story: 'The Gun Show' host Mike 'Gunz' Gunzelman discusses four opening acts quitting Ed Sheeran's concert tour after Macklemore was dropped. Gunzelman analyzes online pressure on performers to take political positions and compares the music industry reaction to 2024 college campus demonstrations.
Hannah Einbinder has taken aim at Ed Sheeran amid the growing backlash over Macklemore’s removal from the singer’s U.S. tour.
The "Hacks" star criticized Sheeran on Instagram, joking that she was speaking "as a ginger" before wishing him an especially painful sunburn.
"Ed Sheeran i say this as a ginger. i hope you get a REALLY bad sun burn the kind on the back of your entire body where it hurts to lie down or walk or sit," Einbinder wrote.
MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTIAN STANCE
Hannah Einbinder slammed Ed Sheeran over his Palestinian stance. (Getty Images)
Her post came after Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran’s Loop Tour after onstage comments supporting Palestinians.
Einbinder was among several celebrities to publicly call out Sheeran, who addressed the controversy in a lengthy statement posted Tuesday.

"Macklemore asked to join my tour last year and I agreed, because I respect him as an artist," Sheeran wrote on social media. "As with all my support acts, I agree that they play a setlist of their choosing."

On Monday, Macklemore had claimed that Sheeran told him Robert Kraft, the owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, had rallied other stadium owners to oppose allowing the rapper to perform. According to his account, the venues allegedly gave Sheeran an ultimatum: "If Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues."

Sheeran’s statement offered a different account of the events, saying that, after Macklemore’s performances at his New Jersey shows, venues scheduled for upcoming tour dates told organizers they would pull the shows if Macklemore remained on the lineup.
"After Macklemore’s performances at my New Jersey shows, venues on my upcoming tour dates communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting," Sheeran wrote.

"I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said. I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft. I was also involved in direct talks with promoters along with activists on both sides to try and find a mutual resolution for all, but the venue’s and promoter’s decision was final."

Macklemore was kicked off Sheeran's tour due to his pro-Palestinian remarks.  (Kevin Mazur/WireImage)

Sheeran said he has deliberately avoided using his professional platform for politics because his audience includes young people and children from diverse backgrounds. Sheeran said concertgoers attend his shows expecting "a place of safety and sanctuary" rather than a political forum.

"There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics – my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds," he wrote. "Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace.

"I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change."
Sheeran also rejected the suggestion that his decision not to speak publicly about his personal beliefs made him indifferent to the conflict.

"I am not complicit," he wrote. "I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care."
MICK JAGGER DOESN'T WANT TO 'LECTURE' FANS, SAYS HIS JOB IS TO MAKE PEOPLE 'HAVE THE BEST TIME'
However, his statement has done little to quiet the criticism.

"Wicked" actor Marissa Bode accused Sheeran of lacking a backbone, writing that although she uses a wheelchair, she still has a "f---ing spine," before adding her support for Palestinians on Instagram.
"Ed Sheeran, my legs may not work like they used to before, but at least I have a f---ing spine. Free Palestine, b----," she wrote.
Marissa Bode slammed Sheeran, calling him a "b----." (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images)
Children’s educator and YouTube sensation Ms. Rachel similarly said Sheeran had "caved" to people who opposed Macklemore’s advocacy and argued that silence over Gaza is not neutral.

"Ed Sheeran had an opportunity [to] show that we won’t be bullied into punishing people for supporting Palestine. Instead he caved to people who refuse to accept what the world knows. A genocide is happening in Gaza. We all need to speak out against it."

PAUL MCCARTNEY SAYS BEATLES CLASSIC UNITES AUDIENCES 'IN TRUMP’S AMERICA' DESPITE POLITICAL DIVIDE

Former Pink Floyd member Roger Waters delivered one of the harshest responses, posting a video in which he contrasted Macklemore’s willingness to speak out with Sheeran’s refusal to take a public position.

"I just have a little message for you," he said in a video he shared on social media. "There are two kinds of people in this world, Ed. There are people who do the right thing. That rapper Macklemore would be one of those people. And there are people, many of them sadly little – excuse me, I nearly used the F-word then, p------ like you who do the wrong thing. Goodbye."
Macklemore has also criticized Sheeran’s stance, though he said their friendship was not necessarily over.

He argued that Sheeran could not move beyond his public position of "not taking sides," adding that refusing to choose a side in an unequal conflict does not amount to neutrality.

Responding to Macklemore's claims, Sheeran said he was "not complicit."  (Dia Dipasupil)
Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Irish folk band Beoga all announced that they would withdraw from upcoming dates in solidarity with Macklemore.
Finneas said artists should not be silenced when speaking for oppressed people, while Rowe condemned the use of wealth and venue power to suppress pro-Palestinian voices.
Lukas Graham wrote that he was grateful for his friendship with Sheeran but couldn't "carry on with tour as things stand" before withdrawing.
"I'm sorry we won't be there. This is a difficult decision, but it's one I need to stand by," Graham added.
Macklemore has been speaking about Palestinians for three years and said now is not the time to be silenced.  (Fox News Digital)

A week after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" while opening for Sheeran, the rapper was dropped from the remaining U.S. dates he was scheduled to perform on the "Shape of You" singer's tour.

"As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans," Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s Loop Tour, said in a statement to Rolling Stone.
"After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates."
While Macklemore said he hopes his relationship with Sheeran won't crumble over this, he stands by his position.

title: Jelly Roll says he could walk away from country music if God tells him to: ‘Y’all will never see me again’
summary: After three Grammys, a Grand Ole Opry membership and his divorce from Bunnie Xo, Jelly Roll says he may walk away from country music for good.
story: Jelly Roll tells Fox News Digital what it means to him to celebrate the 60th Academy of Country Music Awards.
Jelly Roll isn't ruling out walking away from country music altogether.
The Grammy-winning singer revealed that if God calls him to a different purpose, he could leave the music business behind — and fans might never see him again.

The "Son of a Sinner" singer made the candid admission in a previously recorded interview with "Y’all Access Radio’s" Kelly Sutton while backstage at the Grand Ole Opry in March. The interview was published on Sept. 13.

"Everything that Jason or Jelly Roll wanted to do in the music business, I’ve done now, so at this point, I really need to go talk to God and see if he wants me to stick around, or what he wants me to do next," Jelly Roll, whose real name is Jason DeFord, said.

"If God tells me to go work at a homeless shelter in Paducah, Ky., I’m outta here, you know what I'm saying? Y’all will never see me again, and I’ll be working at a… he gave me everything I ever wanted, man — Grammys, ACMs, CMAs, I’m a member of the Grand Ole Opry, like God has done it."

But now he says he's trying to figure out whether music is still where he's supposed to be.

Guest host Jelly Roll appears on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" on Aug. 26. (Disney via Getty Images)
The comments follow an eventful year for the country star, including changes in his personal life and major career milestones.
Jelly Roll also drew political backlash this summer after guest-hosting "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" and taking aim at President Donald Trump's weight, physical fitness and approval ratings.

title: Macklemore's long history of controversy from Grammy wins to 'Free Palestine' concert remarks
summary: Macklemore's pro-Palestinian concert remarks and controversial moments long predate his removal from Ed Sheeran's "Loop Tour" over his "Hind's Hall" performance.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Macklemore's activism began long before his pro-Palestinian plight during Ed Sheeran's "Loop Tour."
The musician, who's full name is Ben Haggerty, was kicked off Sheeran's tour following backlash from his "Free Palestine" messaging during his opening act at MetLife Stadium over the weekend.
While the fallout continues now that four supporting acts have withdrawn from the tour, Macklemore, 43, is no stranger to controversy and has often used his platform to amplify political issues.
ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO 'BUILD A BRIDGE' OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO
Macklemore has a long history of using his public platform to amplify activism. (Arnaud Finistre)
The artist broke into the mainstream music scene in 2012 with the release of "The Heist," his debut studio album as the duo Macklemore & Ryan Lewis.

He faced criticism for sweeping the 2014 Grammys with four awards, which included winning the Best Rap Album Grammy over fan favorite Kendrick Lamar, who was equally nominated for seven awards that night.
MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE
Macklemore reached out to Lamar after the show and shared a screenshot of his text on social media where he told the "Humble" rapper that he was "robbed" of the win.

"My text to Kendrick after the show. He deserved best rap album... I'm honored and completely blown away to win anything much less 4 Grammys," Macklemore wrote. "But in that category, he should have won IMO. And that's taking nothing away from The Heist. Just giving GKMC it's proper respect."
More than 30 couples married during a Macklemore & Ryan Lewis performance of "Same Love" at the 2014 Grammy Awards. (Robert Gauthier)
Macklemore & Ryan Lewis sang with Madonna at the 2014 Grammy Awards where Queen Latifah presided over dozens of same-sex and heterosexual weddings during the performance. (Cliff Lipson)

He added, "With that being said, thank you to the fans. You're the reason we were on that stage tonight. And to play Same Love on that platform was a career highlight. The greatest honor of all. That's what this is about. Progress and art. Thank you."

Grammy viewers witnessed Macklemore & Ryan Lewis perform "Same Love" on stage to a mass wedding between 33 same-sex and heterosexual couples, officiated by Queen Latifah. At the end of the performance, Madonna appeared on stage for a rendition of her song, "Open Your Heart."

That same year, Macklemore faced backlash following an appearance with Ryan Lewis at The Museum of Pop Culture in Seattle, where he wore a black wig, beard and fake nose, which some claimed was an antisemitic costume.

Macklemore issued an apology in 2014 after appearing in what critics called an antisemitic costume at an event in Seattle. (Suzi Pratt)

"Family, friends and fans alike who know me well, know that I'm absolutely not the person described in certain headlines today," he wrote on his website. "There is no worse feeling than being misunderstood, especially when people are hurt or offended."

"I respect all cultures and all people," he continued. "I would never intentionally put down anybody for the fabric that makes them who they are. I love human beings, love originality, and ... happen to love a weird outfit from time to time."
He also posted on X, "A fake witches nose, wig, and beard = random costume. Not my idea of a stereotype of anybody."

In 2023, he was one of many who signed the Arists4Ceasefire letter in support of Palestinian rights and humanitarian aid for Gaza and the following year released "Hind's Hall," an anthem supporting pro-Palestinian student protestors.
During a performance at Seattle's Palestine Will Live Forever festival, Macklemore faced heavy criticism after leading an anti-U.S. chant where he encouraged the crowd to say, "F- - - America."
Macklemore was one of many who signed the Arists4Ceasefire letter in support of Palestinian rights and humanitarian aid for Gaza. (Kieran Frost/Redferns)

"My thoughts and feelings are not always expressed perfectly or politely," he said on social media at the time. "Sometimes I slip up and get caught in the moment. Saturday night was one of those times.

Macklemore admitted that he "lost endorsements, I've lost shows, I've lost business ties," but that his support remained "unwavering."

title: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle’s school-run problems shouldn’t 'come as a surprise,’ royal expert says
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle switched Archie and Lili's school after just two days, but royal experts say the traffic issues were entirely predictable.
story: Fox News senior foreign affairs correspondent Greg Palkot reports on Prince Harry and Meghan Markle relocating to the United Kingdom after residing in California for six years, noting that the couple plans to establish a residence outside London and enroll their children in a British school while King Charles undergoes cancer treatment.

None of the security and logistical concerns that forced Prince Harry and Meghan Markle to switch the school their children were attending in England should have been a surprise, according to royal experts.

"The logistics haven’t changed since Harry and Meghan plotted their U.K. return," Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital. "None of this should have come as a surprise."

Schofield said that her sources were warning her about the traffic around the school two weeks ago, "before Archie and Lili had even started. When I spoke to people locally, the school-run traffic was one of the very first issues they raised with me."
The royal couple moved their family from California to the Cotswolds, outside of London, late last month.
PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE’S SCHOOL WARNING LETTERS REIGNITE PRIVACY BATTLE THEY ‘CANNOT CONTROL’: EXPERTS

story: Sally Field told Fox News Digital after her Emmy Award win on Monday night that she "never" stopped loving Dolly Parton.
Sally Field remembers shopping with Dolly Parton at Walmart like it was yesterday.

"She was a friend. I admired her. I loved working with her. I never stopped loving her. title: Tom Cruise admits rumors about his 'intense' behavior on movie sets are true
summary: Tom Cruise told GQ the rumors about his intense on-set behavior are true, revealing what he tells collaborators before they sign on to work with him.
story: The former "Dancing with the Stars" co-host nearly crushed the actor with a motorcycle before he saved the day.
Tom Cruise is confirming what Hollywood has whispered about for years — he really is that intense.
The actor, 64, acknowledged his demanding reputation on movie sets and said he makes sure collaborators know exactly what they're getting into.
"I expect a lot and I'm up-front about it," Cruise said during a GQ cover interview. "It's like: 'The rumors are true. And do you want this?'"
BEAU BRIDGES SAYS TOM CRUISE ‘GETS BETTER WITH AGE’ AS ‘TOP GUN' STAR KEEPS DEFYING HOLLYWOOD ODDS
Tom Cruise confronts rumors about his intense reputation behind the scenes. (Mario Sorrenti / GQ)
"Trust me, the rumors are true. I'll be here before you. What experience do you want?" he laughed.
The actor made clear that his intensity isn't an act he puts on once the cameras start rolling.
"Even when I was a kid, they were like, 'Oh, come on, Tom. You're so intense.' I'm like, 'I don't know what to say. I am intense,'" Cruise remarked.
"I got a very good sense of humor about it," he added.
The Hollywood star makes a surprising admission about his movie-set behavior. (Mario Sorrenti / GQ)
For Cruise, the intensity comes from curiosity and a desire to master his craft.
"When I'm interested in something, I want to learn it. I want to understand it," he said. "And you want to blast through the confusion and kind of build up that ability."
MATT DAMON REFUSES TO PUT BODY IN 'DANGEROUS' SITUATIONS FOR HOLLYWOOD ROLES AFTER TURNING 50
That mindset has helped turn Cruise into one of Hollywood's most famous action stars, but he insisted filmmaking is about much more than spectacular stunts or box-office numbers.
"I say, 'Understand the tools, then go create what you want to create,'" he said.
The "Top Gun" star also discussed the idea that movies are simply another form of entertainment competing with television and streaming.
Tom Cruise poses for the cover of GQ wearing a cowboy hat, T-shirt and jeans. (Mario Sorrenti / GQ)

"I have nothing against cable or TV or Netflix. I think it's great. Create jobs and everything," Cruise said. "But what I like about cinema is it is all of us coming together in a room and sharing an experience."
When Cruise is not on a movie set, he said he's preparing for the next project.
TOM CRUISE SAVED SAMANTHA HARRIS FROM GETTING CRUSHED BY A '500-POUND' MOTORCYCLE
"You know what? I'm preparing for the next. I'm always studying something. I'm always learning something, always."
Cruise stressed that the work behind a movie can begin years before production.
"Movies don't just start when you're shooting it and on a movie set. There's sometimes years of preparation," he said.
Tom Cruise sits on a red Ducati motorcycle outdoors. (Mario Sorrenti / GQ)
During his decades-long career, Cruise has ridden a motorcycle off a cliff, hung from aircraft in midair and performed other death-defying feats for his movies.
Cruise was asked whether he fears death when performing his movie stunts.
"Look, I think you could look at my life and go: I like standing on the edge of a cliff physically and metaphorically," he told GQ.

"Meaning, I look at life as an adventure, and I always have, my whole life. I want to understand people. I want to understand life and cultures. We're looking at life. I wonder: Who are those people? How do they feel? Do they think the way I do? Do they laugh at the same thing? How do I connect with them? And I didn't want to just be a tourist. I wanted to go make movies there because I also find you really get to know people when you create with them."
Tom Cruise in "Top Gun," in 1986. (Corbis via Getty Images)
He added, "Everyone has a different subjective reality of what they think about life, about people. And there is common ground in humanity, and I'm looking for that common ground."

title: Ed Sheeran says he tried to ‘build a bridge’ over Macklemore tour spot before venues said no
summary: Ed Sheeran says Macklemore's removal from his "Loop Tour" was the concert promoter's decision, not his, after U.S. venues threatened to pull shows.
story: Host of 'The Ben Shapiro Show' Ben Shapiro joins Bill Hemmer and Dana Perino to discuss Macklemore being dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour following his pro-Palestinian comments and Robert Kraft's response. He also reacts to Mahmoud Khalil's lawsuit against Columbia University.
Ed Sheeran addressed Macklemore’s removal from his U.S. tour Tuesday, saying the rapper’s departure was ultimately a decision made by the concert promoter and venues — not by him.

The "Shape of You" singer said he was "appalled" by the conflict between Israel and Palestine and described the suffering on both sides as "a human tragedy," according to a lengthy statement shared on Instagram after Macklemore accused Sheeran and tour organizers of sidelining him over his pro-Palestinian remarks.
Following Sheeran's note, four supporting acts withdrew from the Loop Tour in solidarity with Macklemore, including Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga, Lukas Graham, and Finneas.
MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE
Ed Sheeran responds to Macklemore's claims over tour removal. (Getty Images)
"Macklemore asked to join my tour last year and I agreed, because I respect him as an artist," Sheeran wrote. "As with all my support acts, I agree that they play a setlist of their choosing."

On Monday, Macklemore had claimed that Sheeran told him Robert Kraft, the owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, had rallied other stadium owners to oppose allowing the rapper to perform. According to his account, the venues allegedly gave Sheeran an ultimatum: "if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues."

Sheeran’s statement offered a different account of the events, saying that after Macklemore’s performances at his New Jersey shows, venues scheduled for upcoming tour dates told organizers they would pull the shows if Macklemore remained on the lineup.

"After Macklemore’s performances at my New Jersey shows, venues on my upcoming tour dates communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting," Sheeran wrote. "I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said. I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft. I was also involved in direct talks with promoters along with activists on both sides to try and find a mutual resolution for all, but the venue’s and promoter’s decision was final."
MICHAEL RAPAPORT SLAMS 'CLOWN' MACKLEMORE FOR ANTI-ISRAEL PERFORMANCE
"Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine," Sheeran added. "Macklemore’s contract for the tour was with the promoter, not me."
Macklemore was scheduled to perform at eight of the remaining U.S. dates on Sheeran’s "Loop Tour."
Macklemore was kicked off Ed Sheeran's stadium tour over his "Free Palestine" remarks. (Getty Images)

Sheeran said he has deliberately avoided using his professional platform for politics because his audience includes young people and children from diverse backgrounds. Sheeran said concertgoers attend his shows expecting "a place of safety and sanctuary" rather than a political forum.

"There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics – my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds," he wrote. "Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace. I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change."
Sheeran also rejected the suggestion that his decision not to speak publicly about his personal beliefs made him indifferent to the conflict.

"I am not complicit," he wrote. "I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care."
Mackelmore was slated for a string of performances on Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour. (Kevin Mazur/WireImage)
CHRIS ROBINSON, BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN FACE BACKLASH AS 'AMERICANS HAVE HAD ENOUGH' OF BEING LECTURED: EXPERT
The singer said he spent the week attempting to preserve the tour while balancing the concerns of venues, promoters, fans, crew members and support acts.
"I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living," Sheeran wrote.
He concluded by saying he had tried to find a solution but was ultimately unable to do so.

"I have spent this week trying to build bridges, to find a solution and unfortunately, was unable to do so. I know who I am, both as a person and as an artist, and those who know my heart know my values too."
The message was heard by many, including Billie Eilish's brother, Finneas, who was slated to tour with Sheeran in South America later this year.
A post shared by FINNEAS (@finneas)
A post shared by aaron rowe (@aaronrowe__)
"Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed," he wrote. "I have decided to withdraw from my upcoming tour dates with Ed Sheeran. I stand with Palestine and its people."
Aaron Rowe wrote that the decision wasn't made "lightly" in a similar statement on social media as he withdrew from the tour.

"Ed has been a friend to me and has changed my life, I could never thank him enough for this," Rowe said. "But as Irish people we know all too well about genocide, forced famine and violent occupation."

"I cannot stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power to silence the rightful voices of those who speak up against Israeli genocide and who highlight the savage murder of children. I would lose all respect for myself to carry on as normal."
Rowe noted that he needed to "be true to myself and my ancestors who resisted colonization, and fought for a freedom that I enjoy today in Ireland."
Macklemore claimed he's been vocal about his Palestinian stance for years.  (Morgan Hancock/Getty Images)

"We are a traditional Irish band who never saw ourselves playing in stadiums of that size and that opportunity is not los on us," Beoga wrote on social media. "We have been friends with Ed for over 10 years now and will continue to be. We believe in dialogue as a means of progressing the plight of the Palestinian people."
Lukas Graham wrote that he was grateful for his friendship with Sheeran, but couldn't "carry on with tour as things stand," before withdrawing.
"I'm sorry we won't be there. This is a difficult decision, but it's one I need to stand by," Graham added.

A week after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" while opening for Sheeran, the rapper was dropped from the remaining U.S. dates he was scheduled to perform on the "Shape of You" singer's tour.
A post shared by Beoga (@beogamusic)

"As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans," Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s "Loop Tour," said in a statement to Rolling Stone. "After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates."
On Monday, Macklemore addressed the announcement and doubled down on his stance.

"I’m not sure how to start this. So I’m going to speak from the heart and share the truth," he wrote in a lengthy Instagram statement. "Ed Sheeran and his team have made the decision to remove me from The Loop tour. But before I get into it, I want to say something that should be obvious. In this moment I think it matters. I am not a victim. Ed Sheeran is not a victim. Pink is not a victim. We have careers, money, opportunities, safety and audiences around the world. Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families."
A post shared by Lukas Graham (@lukasgraham)
PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS

"The victims are the Palestinian people. The men, women and children who have been killed, starved, displaced and forced to live through unimaginable violence. More than 20,000 children have been killed in Gaza alone. People are being killed today, and people will be killed tomorrow. I want to make sure that as I tell this story, we don’t lose sight of that."
The rapper claimed Kraft told Sheeran that Macklemore "would not be allowed" to perform at the stadium.

Kraft issued a statement defending his decision to influence the rapper's removal from the tour.
The rapper said now is not the time to be silenced.  (ARNAUD FINISTRE / AFP via Getty Images)

"Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech," the statement read. "Based on Macklemore’s recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line."

The statement continued, "This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real. But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas, a United States and globally (including Canada, European Union, United Kingdom, and Japan) designated terrorist organization whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike. I agree with Macklemore. Too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering, but only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate. Over many decades, I have directed resources to Palestine and created athletic and entrepreneurial opportunities for Palestinians who I admire and respect. Standing with the Palestinian people and standing against Hamas, antisemitism and hate should not be mutually exclusive."

"Much of my time and attention for the last decade has been focused on the fight against antisemitism and hate of all kinds, and I feel a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed. I have tremendous respect for Ed and his music, particularly his unique ability to bring people together and spread joy, and I have always been proud to welcome him and his fans to Gillette Stadium.
"I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same – peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate."
New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft refused to allow Mackelmore at his Gillette stadium. (Kirby Lee/Imagn Images)
While Macklemore said he hopes his relationship with Sheeran won't crumble over this, he stands by his position.

"I didn’t need 10 shows from Ed. I needed 2. Two chances to stand in front of 90,000 people and say the words that somehow became too dangerous to say. Free Palestine. title: Savannah Guthrie thanks Allison Janney after emotional Emmy tribute: 'Our family is in such pain'
summary: Savannah Guthrie got emotional on "Today" after Allison Janney used her Emmys press room victory moment to send love to the Guthrie family and honor missing mom Nancy.
story: The disappearance of Nancy Guthrie, mother of television host Savannah Guthrie, remains under investigation. Alleged kidnappers demanded $4 million in Bitcoin and claimed she ‘perished’ after being abducted. Newly released ransom notes and other evidence are providing investigators with fresh clues as the case remains ongoing.
Savannah Guthrie became emotional after Allison Janney used her Emmy press room moment to express support for Guthrie’s family and remember her missing mother, Nancy Guthrie.

Janney, who won the Emmy for outstanding supporting actress in a drama series for her role in "The Diplomat" at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards on Monday, spoke about Nancy while talking with reporters backstage.

"I honestly can say I think about her every day, and think about the loss and what Savannah and her family are going through," Janney said. "I don’t think I’m alone. I think all of America is thinking about her."
Guthrie later thanked Janney during an emotional conversation on the "Today" show.
SAVANNAH GUTHRIE PLEADS FOR TIPS AS RANSOM NOTE CLAIMS MOM IS DEAD: 'SOMEBODY KNOWS SOMETHING'
Savannah Guthrie became emotional over Allison Janney's message of support. (Getty Images)
"I was so touched to see her do that," Savannah said. "It was her moment, her triumph. For her to sit and just take a moment to think about our family — it meant so much."
She said she never misses an opportunity to talk about her mother and the pain her family continues to endure.
"I never let a moment pass if I get one to talk about my mom, how much I miss her and love her," she said. "My whole family is in such pain. We need help."
"Thank you, Allison Janney, for remembering us and giving me an opportunity to renew that call," Savannah continued. "We just want our mom home to give her a proper goodbye. That’s all."

Nancy, the 84-year-old mother of Savannah, was taken from her home in Tucson's upscale Catalina Foothills neighborhood in the early hours of Feb. 1, according to the Pima County Sheriff's Department and the FBI.
Savannah Guthrie poses alongside her mother Nancy Guthrie during a production break whilst hosting NBC's "Today Show" live from Australia. (Don Arnold/WireImage)

title: Nick Reiner won't face death penalty in Rob, Michele Reiner murder case
summary: Nick Reiner returns to court Tuesday as proceedings continue in the case involving the alleged killings of his parents, Rob and Michele Reiner.
story: Death penalty will not be sought against Rob, Michele Reiner's son in double murder trial
All eyes were on Nick Reiner Tuesday when he returned to court for the latest proceedings in his criminal case.

Reiner is accused of killing his parents, Rob and Michele Reiner. Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan J. Hochman announced Tuesday that prosecutors will not seek the death penalty in the case during a press conference ahead of Reiner’s court hearing.

"In deciding whether or not the DA's office was going to seek the death penalty, we have gone through a rigorous review where we look at the aggravating factors, as well as the mitigating factors – where we have spoken to the victims' family, we have spoken to prosecutors, law enforcement, and I've worked with the most senior people in the district attorney's office," Hochman told reporters Tuesday. "After a careful and thorough review of all these factors, the District Attorney's office will not be seeking the death penalty in this case. That means that the maximum sentence that Mr. Reiner will be looking at is life without the possibility of parole."
NICK REINER INDICTED IN MURDERS OF PARENTS ROB, MICHELE REINER AT BRENTWOOD HOME
Nick Reiner is set to return to court as he faces accusations of killing his parents, Rob and Michele Reiner, at their Brentwood home. (Chris Torres/Pool via Reuters)

Reiner was charged with two counts of murder and included special circumstance allegations of multiple murders and lying in wait after a grand jury indictment. Prosecutors also alleged he used a knife.
"This was a profound betrayal by someone who was loved and trusted by the very people he is accused of killing," Los Angeles County District Attorney Hochman said at the time.
During Tuesday's press conference, Hochman revealed Nick's siblings have petitioned for the grand jury transcripts to be sealed.

"…they have expressed a strong desire for these transcripts to remain sealed," he told reporters. "And they basically have said that the disclosure to the public and the media of the details and evidence of the killing of their parents will cause them additional trauma and harm, and they have respectfully asked for the court to keep the transcript sealed."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
WATCH: NICK REINER CASE MAY TAKE YEARS TO GO TO TRIAL, LEGAL EXPERT SAYS
Hochman hinted Nick's defense plans to file a motion to dismiss, although it hasn't occurred yet.
"We estimate that the trial will not occur before 2027," he said. "However, when the defense is ready to proceed, the government … will be ready to proceed."

Nick's Tuesday court hearing lasted 15 minutes. He entered the courtroom at a brisk pace, clean-shaven with slightly unkempt hair and dressed in a brown jumpsuit. He remained attentive throughout the hearing, his hands cuffed to the chair. Reiner spoke only a few times, responding directly to Superior Court Judge Sam Ohta as the judge explained his speedy-trial rights. He answered the judge’s questions with brief replies, including "yes" and "yes, I do."
WATCH: LA COUNTY DA VOWS TO CONVICT NICK REINER IN ROB AND MICHELE REINER MURDER CASE
Prosecutors allege Reiner fatally stabbed his father, 78, and mother, 70, on Dec. 14, 2025, at their Brentwood home.

As his criminal case moves forward, Reiner has demanded access to funds from a trust worth as much as $1.5 million after he was allegedly denied access to money he says he is entitled to use, including to hire high-profile defense attorney Alan Jackson.
Prosecutors charged Nick Reiner with two counts of murder, alleging he used a knife and waited to carry out the killings. (Michael Buckner/Getty Images for Teen Vogue)
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Months after Reiner was put behind bars in connection to the murder of his parents, he filed a petition arguing that the person appointed to oversee his $1.5 million trust has unlawfully withheld funds that are already legally his. Reiner insisted he needed the trust money to pay for criminal defense counsel and basic necessities while incarcerated.

Jackson, who previously represented Karen Read, began working on the case immediately after Reiner's arrest, but the representation endeed when anticipated family funding failed to materialize. In a declaration, Jackson said his firm remained willing to return if funding became available, including through alternative fee arrangements.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
As the case moves forward, Nick Reiner is seeking access to his $1.5 million trust fund to help pay for his defense and basic necessities. (Stefanie Keenan)

Los Angeles Fire Department officials responded to a Brentwood-area home at around 3:30 p.m. on Dec. 14, where two bodies were discovered. Officials later confirmed the bodies to be of Rob and his wife, Michele.

"Both victims were found in the master bedroom of the area of the home," LAPD Assistant Police Chief Dominic Choi later confirmed during an LAPD Board of Police Commissioners meeting. Officers then conducted a "thorough search" of the residence and found no additional victims or suspects.

title: Taylor Swift steals Emmys spotlight, watches husband Travis Kelce's Chiefs game with Tom Cruise
summary: Taylor Swift skipped the 2026 Emmys to watch husband Travis Kelce with Tom Cruise, but still stole the show in a hilarious "SVU" spoof with host Mariska Hargitay.

Taylor Swift skipped the 2026 Emmy Awards, but made sure to leave her mark on television's biggest night.
Swift, 36, still surprised the audience with a special appearance alongside her longtime friend and Emmys host, Mariska Hargitay, in a prerecorded "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit" spoof.

As the 78th Emmy Awards were underway in Los Angeles, the "Lover" singer was spotted chatting it up with Tom Cruise at Arrowhead Stadium while supporting her husband, Travis Kelce, at the Kansas City Chiefs game.

Tom Cruise previously supported the "Reputation" singer at one of her Eras Tour stops in London. (Jamie Squire/Getty Images)

"Now, in order to crack a Swiftie case, you got to think like a Swiftie, because the Swifties think that everything is a clue to what she’ll do next," Hargitay said while navigating an evidence board.
As the team attempted to tie information together, a voice chimed in, "Hey guys, this isn't adding up."
Taylor Swift made a guest appearance in an Emmys spoof with host Mariska Hargitay of "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit." (Patrick T. Fallon/Getty Images)

As the investigation played out, Hargitay determined, "Taylor Swift will not be at the Emmys."
Swift chimed in, "Maybe she’s going to do one of those cool pre-taped sketch things to support the host."
The camera panned toward the pair where the "Reputation" singer was shown holding her Scottish Fold cat named Olivia Benson, an homage to her favorite "SVU" character.

title: Prince Harry's first birthday back in Britain unlikely to bring reconciliation with the royal family: experts
summary: Royal experts reveal how Meghan Markle and the children will mark Prince Harry's first birthday back in Britain amid unresolved family tensions.
story: British royals expert Hilary Fordwich reveals how Prince Harry may spend his birthday and discusses where he stands with his father and brother.
Prince Harry "will likely hear" from King Charles III on his birthday, but "don’t expect some grand royal reunion," according to a royal expert.

Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital that the prince would probably have a celebration "similar to what we recently saw from Meghan Markle. Singing and dancing in the kitchen. Party hats for the pups."

"I imagine Harry will keep it relatively private with Meghan and the children," she added. "Being back in Britain makes this birthday significant, but I don’t expect some grand royal reunion. There is still far too much unresolved behind the scenes."
QUEEN CAMILLA PUTS PAST DIFFERENCES WITH PRINCE HARRY ASIDE AS KING CHARLES SEEKS CLOSER FAMILY TIES: EXPERTS
Prince Harry is celebrating his 42nd birthday on Sept. 15 back in England. (Getty Images)
Harry is celebrating his first birthday — he turns 42 on Sept. 15 — since the couple returned to his home country from California after six years late last month.
"Harry will likely hear from his father on his birthday," Schofield said. "He will most definitely chat with his uncle, Earl Spencer, and aunts, Lady Sarah McCorquodale and Lady Jane Fellowes."
PRINCE WILLIAM AND KATE MIDDLETON 'PLAYING IT COOL' AS PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE RETURN TO THE UK: EXPERT

She added that birthdays "have a way of reminding you who is in your life and who isn’t. Harry may be physically closer to his family, but emotionally, there is still enormous distance there. Moving back to Britain doesn’t automatically repair years of broken trust."
"Being back in Britain makes this birthday significant, but I don’t expect some grand royal reunion. There is still far too much unresolved behind the scenes."
Schofield noted that the Spencer side of the family — Princess Diana’s — "seems to be embracing him."
PRINCE WILLIAM ‘BLINDSIDED’ BY HARRY, MEGHAN RETURN AS KATE FEARS NEW TURMOIL FROM ROYAL FEUD: EXPERTS

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will likely have a small family celebration for his birthday, experts said. (Getty Images)

title: Dolly Parton, Rob Reiner receive emotional tributes during 2026 Emmy Awards
summary: Sally Field delivered an emotional tribute to Dolly Parton at the 2026 Emmy Awards, calling her "Steel Magnolias" co-star an angel on earth.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Sally Field reflected on Dolly Parton's legacy during a moving tribute to the late country music legend at the 2026 Emmy Awards in Los Angeles, Calif.
"If there are truly angels on earth, then we just lost one, Dolly Parton," Field confessed of her "Steel Magnolias" co-star.
Parton died on Aug. 25 following a "brief battle with cancer," according to her representatives. She was 80.
DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY
Dolly Parton and Rob Reiner were each honored during the 78th Emmy Awards in Los Angeles, Calif., on Monday. (Getty Images)

"It was my great, good fortune to have worked with Dolly in a film called 'Steel Magnolias,' and over the years I never stopped loving her though we lived very far apart," Field told the audience at the Peacock Theater. "I adored her from day one, how could you not?"
"She was genuine, and humble, supportive and blisteringly funny with a bawdy sense of humor that would send any rude guy looking for a place to hide."
CARRIE UNDERWOOD HONORS DOLLY PARTON'S FAITH AND LEGACY DURING EMOTIONAL CONCERT TRIBUTE
Reba McEntire performed a rendition of Parton's '83 hit, "Appalachian Memories." (Patrick T. Fallon)
Field, 79, admitted that she "couldn't see then what a real giant Dolly was."

"Not just as an artist, but as a human ... She was a humanitarian whose contributions had made a profound difference in the lives of so many in her home state of Tennessee, and across our country," Field said.
"God bless you, Dolly Parton, my friend. I am not the only one on earth that will love you forever and ever."
Dolly Parton died in August after a brief battle with cancer. (ABC Photo Archives)

Dressed in a sparkling white gown, Reba McEntire then took the stage to perform a rendition of Parton's classic 1983 song, "Appalachian Memories."
Parton was surrounded by loved ones at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center when she died peacefully in Nashville, Tenn., last month.
With Noah Kahan leading a rendition of "Bridge Over Troubled Water," Jamie Lee Curtis commemorated the life of director Rob Reiner, who died in December alongside his wife, Michele Singer Reiner.

"He now holds the record of 48 years for the longest gap between acting Emmys, which was previously held by his father Carl Reiner at 37 years," Curtis told the crowd through tears.

title: Michael J Fox receives standing ovation at 2026 Emmys for Parkinson's disease advocacy work
summary: Michael J. Fox received a standing ovation at the 2026 Emmys alongside wife Tracy Pollan, revealing his foundation is "close" to a Parkinson's cure.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Michael J. Fox was honored with the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award at the 2026 Emmys for his advocacy and philanthropic work supporting Parkinson’s disease research.

The Bob Hope Humanitarian Award is an honorary Emmy presented by the Television Academy and the Bob & Dolores Hope Foundation. Established in 2002, it recognizes a television-industry figure whose philanthropic work has made a lasting impact on society.
Fox attended the award show on Monday night with his wife, Tracy Pollan. This was the couple's first appearance at the Emmy Awards in 13 years.
Michael J. Fox at the 78th Emmy Awards held at Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026, in Los Angeles, California. (Rich Polk/Variety via Getty Images)

Fox received a standing ovation as he took the stage and talked about his Parkinson’s diagnosis. Fox was diagnosed with young-onset Parkinson’s disease in 1991 at age 29. He publicly revealed his diagnosis in 1998.

On the Emmy Awards' stage, Fox said, "Initially, I kept my Parkinson's diagnosis a secret. I worried that it would affect my work and my relationship with audiences."
Michael J. Fox accepts the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award. (NBC via Getty Images)

He continued, "Would they laugh if they knew I was sick? And then I was stunned by the support I got. The support from all of you. It was so uplifting. It made me feel like I could keep doing this, and I hadn't lost what I do, and they couldn't take this away from me. And it's because you stood up for me, and I really appreciate it."
