Less than three weeks later, a 10-year-old girl at Seneca Creek State Park was also attacked while wading with an organized group.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Would-be Trump assassin Thomas Crooks had Snapchat, which may hold evidence 'treasure trove': former FBI agent
summary: A Snapchat account tied to Thomas Crooks could hold a "treasure trove" of evidence, a retired FBI agent says, as Senate files reveal his digital trail.
story: Retired FBI agent Jason Pack tells Fox News Digital that a Snapchat account tied to would-be Trump assassin Thomas Crooks could still hold recoverable evidence, even though the app is known for disappearing messages.

Federal documents turned over to the Senate reveal a Snapchat account tied to Thomas Crooks, the man who attempted to assassinate President Donald Trump, according to the records viewed by Fox News Digital.
The federal documents turned over to the Senate, first reported by the New York Post, revealed that FBI agents located a Snapchat account belonging to Crooks with the username "tom_crooks19."
Crooks killed one person and seriously injured two others during his attempt to assassinate Trump July 13, 2024.

According to the FBI documents, an Amazon account was also located. Crooks also had an account with Mailfence, an encrypted email service, which the documents say he logged into multiple times between April 15, 2024, and July 8, 2024. He also used a Gmail account.
TWO YEARS AFTER BUTLER, THREATS AGAINST TRUMP KEEP ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT IN SHARP FOCUS

Thomas Matthew Crooks was a 20-year-old from Bethel Park, Pa., who attempted to assassinate former President Donald Trump during a 2024 campaign rally before being shot and killed by Secret Service agents. (Associated Press; Fox News Digital)
Retired FBI Supervisory Special Agent Jason Pack told Fox News Digital the Snapchat account may hold a "treasure trove" of evidence.

"When you snap and that picture goes away that everything is gone, and that's not true. When I've served search warrants, there's been a treasure trove of information that has come back," Pack said. "It's not like some people think when you've snapped, and then it goes away, it's totally gone. That's not entirely the case."
SEND US A TIP
Pack said there are certain elements of Crooks' Snapchat account that may not have been recoverable but said there's a "good amount of information in there."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Republican presidential candidate and former President Donald Trump is rushed offstage by U.S. Secret Service agents after being grazed by a bullet during a rally July 13, 2024, in Butler, Pa. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)
TRUMP'S DECADE OF ASSASSINATION THREATS RUNS FROM BUTLER SHOOTING TO LATEST GOLF CLUB BREACH
However, Pack said Crooks was likely careful when using an app like Snapchat, since it's not fully encrypted.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"What you do see is a pattern of trying to hide things and using aliases. And, so, if he's taking that much care to publicly not be seen picking up deliveries and those types of things, you have to assume he's probably taken just as much diligence with his social media and with his digital footprint," he said.

Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump pumps his fist as he is rushed offstage by U.S. Secret Service agents after being grazed by a bullet during a rally on July 13, 2024, in Butler, Pa. (Anna MoneymakerGetty Images)
FBI Director Kash Patel testified Tuesday at a Senate Oversight Committee hearing that there's no evidence that Crooks was linked to anyone else.

"We found no evidence that that individual was literally even speaking to any other human being other than his parents, who he resided with," Patel testified.

title: Nigerian woman in Massachusetts charged after alleged illegal voting in federal elections
summary: Gladys Adaeze Okafor allegedly falsified her citizenship on United States voter registration cards in Massachusetts to illegally cast ballots.
story: Homeland Security Investigations agents execute a major Texas voter fraud crackdown, arresting seven non-citizens in North Texas for illegal voting. U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould pledges to prosecute individuals who lie to the federal government about their citizenship status to cast ballots. The arrests come amid a broader federal push to secure voter rolls and investigate fraudulent registrations ahead of federal elections.
A Nigerian woman living in the United States as a permanent resident in Massachusetts illegally voted in at least two elections after lying about her citizenship, authorities said.

Gladys Adaeze Okafor, 56, has been charged by the Justice Department with unlawfully voting as an alien for allegedly casting ballots in the 2024 presidential primary election and the 2022 midterm elections despite not being a U.S. citizen.
She is expected to appear in a Boston federal courtroom on Wednesday.
CANADIAN NONCITIZEN ACCUSED OF ILLEGALLY VOTING IN FEDERAL AND STATE ELECTIONS

Gladys Adaeze Okafor, 56, is charged with illegally voting in elections despite not being a United States citizen. Okafor, a Nigerian citizen, lives in Massachusetts as a permanent resident, authorities said. (Getty Images; Justice Department)
Okafor repeatedly falsified her citizenship status on official documents under penalty of perjury to gain access to the ballot, federal prosecutors allege.
In July 2022, she submitted a voter registration card and signed her name certifying that she was a U.S. citizen, authorities said. The City of Lynn subsequently registered her to vote.
NONCITIZEN CHARGED WITH VOTING IN MINNESOTA 2024 ELECTION AFTER ADMITTING ‘MISTAKE’ TO INVESTIGATORS

In October 2023, Okafor submitted another voter registration card where she checked a box saying she was an American citizen, prosecutors said. She then voted in the 2024 presidential primary election, court documents state.
Okafor was born in Nigeria and obtained lawful permanent resident status in December 2022. However, she is not a U.S. citizen and has not applied for U.S. citizenship, prosecutors said.
She faces up to a year in prison and up to $10,000 in fines.

Recently, seven noncitizens were indicted in connection with an election integrity investigation in Texas. Earlier this month, the DOJ charged five people in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Wisconsin in cases involving alleged illegal voting or fraudulent registration during the 2022 or 2024 elections.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Taxpayer funds meant for LA homeless allegedly spent on Tahiti trip, nightclub, luxury cars: feds
summary: Three defendants face federal charges in a Los Angeles homeless services fraud crackdown involving alleged wire fraud, bribery and money laundering.
story: Federal officials announced charges against three defendants accused of exploiting programs intended to provide housing and services to homeless Californians, with two arrested Wednesday morning.

Taxpayer dollars intended to put roofs over the heads of Los Angeles’ homeless allegedly paid instead for a Tahiti vacation, a high-end nightclub, luxury vehicles and other personal expenses, federal authorities said Wednesday as agents fanned out across the city in an early-morning fraud crackdown.

At the center of the crackdown is Michael Young, 46, a founder of Culver City-based nonprofit Home At Last, who received more than $118 million in public funds through government contracts, including more than $75 million from the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority, according to the Justice Department.
Prosecutors allege Young misappropriated millions, including more than $7.5 million through a sham vendor scheme.
"The days of these wire fraud experts flying on private jets, driving around Beverly Hills in Range Rovers and doing lavish things is over," HUD Secretary Scott Turner said.
WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT THE NEWSOM-LINKED CHARITIES REPORTEDLY CAUGHT IN DOJ’S SIGHTS
Michael Young, 46, Lakiya Malone, 48, and Donye Mitchell, 55, were charged in the federal fraud crackdown, authorities said Wednesday. (Department of Justice)

Young was one of three defendants charged Wednesday in separate federal cases targeting alleged fraud and corruption involving money intended to house and provide services to homeless Californians. Two were arrested Wednesday, while a third was considered a fugitive.
FBI agents take positions outside the home of Lakiya Malone, who was charged with fraud involving federal homelessness aid programs, in Los Angeles Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)

Prosecutors allege Young used shell companies and fraudulent billing practices to divert taxpayer money, spending more than $1 million to open and operate Six Seven Five Lounge, a high-end Inglewood restaurant and nightclub.
At Wednesday’s news conference, federal officials also accused Young of spending nearly $50,000 on a luxury Tahiti vacation and $140,000 restoring a vintage Chevrolet Impala.
FBI agents take positions outside the home of Lakiya Malone, who was charged with fraud involving federal homelessness aid programs, in Los Angeles Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)
"The taxpayers did not sign up to fund this nightclub," Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald said.
WHITE HOUSE LAUNCHES INTERACTIVE MAP TRACKING BILLIONS IN SUSPECTED FRAUD

Authorities also arrested Lakiya Malone, 48, an employee of Special Service for Groups, on a 21-count indictment alleging she accepted more than $180,000 in bribes and kickbacks from Alexander Soofer, executive director of nonprofit Abundant Blessings.

Lakiya Malone, charged with fraud involving federal homelessness aid programs, walks out of her home toward federal authorities with her hands raised in Los Angeles Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)

In exchange, Malone allegedly provided priority referrals, including "ghost" homeless participants who never lived at the housing sites. Prosecutors allege their files were fabricated using fake welcome letters, forged sign-in sheets and falsified eligibility forms.

Soofer, who was previously charged, has agreed to plead guilty to wire fraud and money laundering. He admitted obtaining $23 million in public money intended to combat homelessness and pocketing at least $2 million for himself and unrelated businesses.
FBI agents stand outside the home of Lakiya Malone, who was charged with fraud involving federal homelessness aid programs, in Los Angeles Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)

A third defendant, Donye Mitchell, 55, CEO of The Big Blue Umbrella, is considered a fugitive. Prosecutors allege he obtained more than $1.2 million in grant funding after making false representations and later used grant money for personal expenses including bail-bond costs, credit card debt, family transfers and PlayStation charges.

"If you or someone you know has defrauded money allocated for the homeless, I suggest you report it to law enforcement," First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said. "If you don’t, your door may be the next one we’re hitting."

title: Lindsay Clancy prosecutors face dilemma: Retrial or plea deal in case involving 3 strangled children
summary: Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney says he'd accept a bench trial on reduced charges, but prosecutors face pressure to retry the hung jury case.
story: Fox News contributor and constitutional legal scholar Jonathan Turley breaks down recent statements from jurors in Lindsay Clancy's mistrial and predicts where the case is headed next.

Prosecutors pursuing a second trial against Lindsay Clancy could face the same obstacle that produced a hung jury the first time: finding 12 Massachusetts jurors willing to unanimously reject her insanity defense.

Jonathan Turley, a Fox News contributor and professor at The George Washington University Law School, said the prosecution must weigh the possibility of another deadlocked trial against the political and emotional consequences of abandoning the case.

"The question is whether they could ever get a jury, particularly in Massachusetts, that would unanimously vote against this defendant," Turley told Fox News Digital. "For prosecutors, they have to weigh that, but they may find the alternative equally unappealing — to simply walk away and say, 'There are three dead children here, but we just don't think we could ever win this case.'"
LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON SIGNALS HE'S OPEN TO A DEAL, HOPES DA WILL 'REVISIT' CASE
Defendant Lindsay Clancy watches jurors enter the courtroom during her murder trial on Friday, Sept. 4, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)

Neama Rahmani, a former federal prosecutor, said he believes the district attorney's office should try and negotiate a deal — but also that it appears unlikely due to the nature of the crime and the defense's position after deadlocked jurors split 11-1, with only a single holdout in favor of finding Clancy guilty of murder in the strangling deaths of her three young children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months.

"The reason I don't think there's any deal to be made here is Reddington has come out during his media tour and said that he's not going to accept any deal that results in jail time," he told Fox News Digital. "Even if you're talking about first-degree or second-degree murder, in Massachusetts, first-degree, of course, has no possibility of parole. Second-degree has the possibility of a parole. That's not something that Reddington and the defense are going to accept."
Lindsay Clancy's defense lawyer, Kevin J. Reddington, addresses the media outside of Plymouth Superior Court, Aug. 26, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
LINDSAY CLANCY'S LAWYER REVEALS POST-MISTRIAL STRATEGY AS RETRIAL LOOMS
The defense does not dispute that Clancy, a 36-year-old former delivery room nurse, choked her three children to death with exercise bands in January 2023. Then she tried to kill herself.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
She survived a fall from a second-story window and is now paralyzed.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
Her defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, has argued that she is not criminally responsible for the deaths due to mental illness or defect.
LINDSAY CLANCY'S ATTORNEY ASKS JUDGE TO ACQUIT HER OUTRIGHT, ENDING CASE AND BARRING A RETRIAL

Still, he's said in recent interviews that he is open to talking about a deal, and he told Fox News' Bryan Llenas last week that if prosecutors reduced the top charge to second-degree murder, he would opt for a bench trial — one without jurors — in the hope that she receives probation as punishment.
GOT A TIP?

"I would like to see [Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz] reduce it to a second-degree so we could possibly waive a jury and try the case before a judge," he said. "I would see Tim determine that the case should not go forward and dismiss it, or in the alternative fashion, something where Lindsay gets the mental, physical help that she needs rather than criminal prosecution — because I would not ever, ever in a million years have that woman go to Framingham State Prison."
District Attorney Timothy Cruz leaves Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

As prosecutors weigh a potential retrial, Judge William Sullivan is protecting the names of jurors in her mistrial, ordering their identities to be impounded indefinitely and the confidential juror questionnaires to be impounded for at least the next 10 days.
JUROR ON LINDSAY CLANCY TRIAL SAYS 'WE LET DOWN LINDSAY' FOLLOWING MISTRIAL
Defendant Lindsay Clancy listens during her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., on July 30, 2026. (CJ Gunther/The Boston Herald via AP, Pool)

He cited threats and concerns for their safety.

title: Friend remembers late Army paratrooper who helped Fox News reporter, Afghans and Helene victims: 'Send me'
summary: Army veteran Sean Michael Lee served with the 82nd Airborne Division and later helped evacuate allies from Afghanistan and set up aid stations in Poland.
story: Steven Rozina, deputy COO of the Independence Fund, honors the life and legacy of the late Sean Michael Lee. An Army paratrooper who served in Iraq and Afghanistan, Lee continued helping others long after leaving the military.
Sean Michael Lee dedicated his life to serving others.

The Army veteran with more than 20 years of military experience spanning multiple deployments and companies — including as a paratrooper for the vaunted 82nd Airborne Division — did not retire his commitment to help others when he finished his military career.
"His entire life was in service to others. Up until the very end, Sean was always thinking of others," Steven Rozina told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview.

Rozina, now the deputy chief operating officer for the nonprofit Independence Fund, which helps provide services and support to wounded veterans, met Lee when he too joined the nonprofit to continue his career of service.
ARMY VETERAN PARATROOPER WHO DEPLOYED TO IRAQ, AFGHANISTAN BEFORE HELPING RESCUE FOX NEWS REPORTER DEAD AT 50
Sean Michael Lee in Iraq. (Fox News)
"He immediately took me under his wing as somebody to teach you how to help others," Rozina told Fox News Digital.
Rozina outlined Lee’s impressive post-military resume, which spanned three continents, in his efforts to continue helping people.

"I think it was 2021, the fall of Afghanistan. Sean answered that call again. He helped evacuate thousands of our Afghan allies, people that worked with us, people that are our friends, that are still our friends today," Rozina explained.
MCCHRYSTAL, BRIDGELAND: WANT TO STRENGTHEN AMERICA? REQUIRE A YEAR OF NATIONAL SERVICE

"He got done with that mission and Sean answered the call again. When Russia invaded Ukraine, he went to Poland," Rozina said. "He helped set up aid stations, helped set supply lines. And even when a Fox News reporter, Benjamin Hall, was injured and was essentially lost, Sean was that guy that helped organize the efforts to bring Benjamin home. Sean was never the guy on the front page of the paper, but he was always there."

Coordinating a rescue operation from Poland via another nonprofit group, Save Our Allies, Lee was instrumental in the efforts to bring Hall home after a Russian attack badly wounded him while he was reporting on the war near Kyiv.
AMERICA'S WOUNDED, STRUGGLING VETERANS GET BRAND-NEW HOMES BUILT BY FLORIDA TEENS

Fox News correspondent Benjamin Hall visited "The Faulkner Focus" with host Harris Faulkner at Fox News Channel Studios on March 15, 2023, in New York City, to discuss his book, "Saved: A War Reporter’s Mission to Make It Home." (Roy Rochlin/Getty Images)
In 2024, Lee again jumped into action when Hurricane Helene devastated parts of the Southeast, including his home state of North Carolina — particularly its western mountains.
"Within a few hours, Sean was in the car, and he was headed up to the mountains," Rozina told Fox News Digital.
9/11 HERO’S MEMORY PRESERVED THROUGH MASSIVE EFFORT TO ‘DO GOOD’ FOR VETS, FIRST RESPONDERS: ‘HIS LEGACY’
"I spent a lot of time with Sean up in the mountains. I got the call, and he needed me to come with him, and we slept in our cars and helped set up aid for different communities," Rozina continued.
However, Rozina explained, "when many of us went home, Sean stayed."

"Sean stayed in the mountains, he lived in tents, stayed with communities that didn't have a lot, helped rebuild family homes, helped rebuild… there was a family store that, it was the only thing that these people had, and he was there, he was always there for somebody else," Rozina explained.
AMERICA'S WOUNDED COPS FIND HOPE, HEALING AND SECOND CHANCE THROUGH OFFICERS WHO REFUSE TO LEAVE THEM BEHIND
Sean Michael Lee. (Fox News)

Lee died Tuesday as a result of cancer he developed from exposure to toxic burn pits during his time deployed in the Middle East. He was still working out how to keep helping people until the very end of his life, Rozina said.

"I have a text message from last week where he's making plans for the next mission. The next thing that he wanted to do to make sure if another hurricane hits North Carolina, how are we going to respond? If an earthquake happens, where are we gonna go and how can we be more efficient? How can we help more people?" Rozina told Fox News Digital.
VETERANS FACE SURPRISING THREAT AFTER CANCER DIAGNOSIS, STUDY REVEALS

"Sean, in his own words, was a good 'idea fairy.' Sean came up with great ideas and really it was... Sean's plans were to be prepared, always be prepared. And it was ideas on how can we be prepared for the next emergency; the next time a veteran needs us, how can [we] incorporate our veteran community into helping others? And that was his goal was really to spread who he was, that 'send me' ethos," Rozina said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Lee's work, through the Independence Fund and through Save Our Allies, was about helping people and using his own gifts and talents to do so, Rozina explained.

When asked what he thought Sean's final message to the world would be, he said, "Any help is still help.""You might feel like you're not doing much, but doing something means a lot. So, do what you can," Rozina said of his late friend. "Do the best you can when you're doing it. And do it with a grateful heart. What Sean did: He did the best he could at everything. And those little things add up in the end. He's touched so many lives. He has blessed a lot of deserving people and I know that his memory is not going to fade."

title: Steel Across America ends its cross-country 9/11 memorial at NY Giants game
summary: Tunnel to Towers' Steel Across America tour carried a 16,900-pound South Tower beam across 38 stops before its emotional finale at MetLife Stadium.
story: The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour concluded its more than 38 stops with a final appearance at Metlife Stadium for a New York Giants game this week.
The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour concluded its more than 38 stops with a final appearance at MetLife Stadium for a New York Giants game this week.

The tour featured a 21-foot steel beam from the South Tower of the World Trade Center. Starting in May, the tour traveled from the East Coast across the U.S. and then went to the New York City area to mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11 before Sunday's last stop.

The 16,900-pound piece of steel – recovered from Ground Zero in the days after the attacks by first responders who rushed to the site – has since become a symbol of the nearly 3,000 civilians, firefighters, police officers, emergency workers and military personnel who died that day.
GIANTS HONOR 9/11 HEROES BEFORE EMOTIONAL SUNDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL OPENER AGAINST COWBOYS
The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America Tour concluded at a Giants game inside Metlife Stadium in New Jersey. (Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America Tour)

"For the past four months, communities across the country have welcomed this sacred piece of American history with incredible emotion," Tunnel to Towers Chairman and CEO Frank Siller said in a press release. "Watching people stand in front of that steel, hugging it, praying over it, weeping, reminds me every single day of why we do this work."
‘THEIR SOULS ARE IN THAT STEEL’: 9/11 BEAM MAKES EMOTIONAL STOP IN INDIANAPOLIS BEFORE RETURN TO NYC
Responders work to clear rubble at Ground Zero in New York City on Oct. 8, 2001. (Ken Tregellas)

An August ceremony in Indianapolis included a color guard, a pipes and drums procession, the national anthem performed by the Voices of the Indianapolis Fire Department and an invocation from Indianapolis Fire Department Chaplain Mike Gatliff.

Indianapolis Fire Division Chief Tom Neal and Timothy Winslow, a retired major general and executive director of the Indiana War Memorial and Museum, also addressed the crowd about the connection between the city’s first responders, veterans and the legacy of 9/11.
9/11 SENT THEM TO WAR. 25 YEARS LATER, VETERANS GRAPPLE WITH WHAT FOLLOWED

"Bringing this steel to Indianapolis, and to a museum that has stood for over a century as a tribute to American sacrifice, is deeply moving," FDNY Lt. Jack Kielty, a Tunnel to Towers board member, said. "Indiana veterans and first responders understand what it means to serve."

Frank Siller, CEO of the Tunnel to Towers Foundation, stands near a piece of World Trade Center steel that was featured during the foundation's effort to honor and remember the victims of the 9/11 attacks as the 25th anniversary approaches. (Courtesy: Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

The event also highlighted Indiana’s own connection to the attacks. Nine Hoosiers died on Sept. 11, while Indianapolis Task Force One sent rescuers to Ground Zero. Six members of the team later died from illnesses linked to their work in the toxic environment, according to the Indiana War Memorial.
Scott Nokes, a Marine Corps veteran and Tunnel to Towers recipient, spoke to attendees about the significance of allowing people to see the steel in person.

"Out of the 2,977 lives that were lost, there’s over 1,000 bodies that were never recovered specifically from Ground Zero in New York," Nokes said. "Their souls are in that steel, and if you touch it, you feel it."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

On the 25th anniversary of 9/11, Frank Siller and his family honored his late brother Stephen Siller — a heroic 34-year-old husband, father and firefighter who, after hearing about the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attack, loaded himself down with gear, and traversed through the Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel on foot heading to the Twin Towers, and ultimately giving his life — by retracing the man's steps.

"This morning’s walk through the Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel was part of the conclusion of Steel Across America, a journey that began four-and-a-half months ago and carried a 21-foot, 16,900-pound World Trade Center steel beam more than 10,500 miles through nearly 40 stops across the country and back, stopping in more than 21 states," a statement from Tunnel to Towers said. "For over four months, the steel has been a gathering place for communities to remember the events of September 11th, to honor first responders and veterans, and to ensure that a new generation understands the significance of what happened 25 years ago."
Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

title: Texas moves to shut down police department over failure to provide 'public benefit to the community'
summary: TCOLE is revoking the Trinidad Police Department's authority to employ officers after finding the agency failed to meet minimum state standards.
story: Jennifer Combs says she was arrested on a felony charge after using Facebook to collect reports about water concerns in Trinidad, Texas. A grand jury later declined to indict her. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)

The Texas Commission on Law Enforcement (TCOLE) is revoking the Trinidad Police Department's authority to appoint or continue employing licensed officers effective Friday, following months of controversy surrounding the small Texas city's police force.
In a Sept. 9 letter to Mayor Dennis Haws, TCOLE said the department "failed to meet minimum standards" and "was unable to provide evidence that the agency provides public benefit to the community."

Regulators also cited deficiencies involving basic resources, including bullet-resistant vests and secure evidence storage, and said the department lacked 18 required policies covering areas such as use of force, vehicle pursuits, professional conduct, active shooters and misconduct investigations.

At a City Council meeting Tuesday night, Interim Police Chief Cameron Beckham blamed previous management for the department's problems and disputed aspects of TCOLE's findings, arguing that many of the deficiencies had since been addressed.
GEORGIA MAYOR FIRES ENTIRE POLICE DEPARTMENT AFTER OFFICERS COMPLAIN ABOUT HIS WIFE IN DISPUTE
Police escort a Texas mother from her home after a Facebook post about Trinidad’s discolored water led to a felony arrest. (Jennifer Combs)
"Piss-poor management is what I'm just going to say," Beckham told the council.

The department has faced scrutiny since May, when Trinidad resident Jennifer Combs was arrested on a felony false alarm or report charge after posting about concerns surrounding the city's water supply.

Combs said in a May 20 Facebook post that she had been collecting residents' photos, videos and accounts of water problems in an effort to document complaints and encourage state investigators to test water at residents' homes. She spent 23 hours in jail before a Henderson County grand jury declined to indict her.

Jennifer Combs says she was arrested on a felony charge after using Facebook to collect reports about water concerns in Trinidad, Texas. A grand jury later declined to indict her. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
Citizen journalist Winston Noles was subsequently arrested and charged with misdemeanor disorderly conduct while protesting outside City Hall. That charge was later dismissed.

Former Police Chief Charles Gregory resigned in June. Combs has since filed a federal lawsuit against the city and Gregory alleging political retaliation. Prior Fox News Digital reporting also documented that former Trinidad Municipal Judge Shellena Bivens was dismissed after throwing out Noles' charge.
TEXAS POLICE ADMIT OFFICER MADE INACCURATE FIRST AMENDMENT REMARKS AFTER PREACHER CITED AT PRIDE EVENT

Henderson County District Judge R. Scott McKee also later questioned the "accuracy, completeness, and reliability" of information Trinidad officers provided while seeking a search warrant connected to Combs' arrest.
The Texas Rangers confirmed in July that they had opened an investigation involving Trinidad but did not disclose its scope.

Haws told Fox News Digital that city leaders will meet with their attorney Friday morning to discuss their next steps. He said the meeting could involve several options rather than being focused solely on keeping the department open.
Police cruisers with the Trinidad Police Department. (Facebook/Trinidad Police Department)
At Tuesday's meeting, Haws said the early meeting time would leave the city time to pursue measures such as an injunction or appeal if advised by counsel.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"We are going to work through this process according to the law and at the direction of our attorney as we go through it," Haws said.
TCOLE's letter also states that revocation does not relieve Trinidad of continuing obligations involving personnel records, 2026 traffic-stop data and unresolved misconduct investigations.
Fox News Digital reached out to TCOLE for further comment.
Bradford Betz is a Fox News Digital breaking reporter covering crime, political issues, and much more.

title: ISIS-K militant sentenced to 20 years for supporting deadly 2021 Abbey Gate bombing
summary: Mohammed Sharifullah admitted to surveilling a route for the Abbey Gate suicide bomber during the chaotic 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal period.
story: Senior advisor to the Secretary of War Sean Parnell honors the heroes of Abbey Gate at a Pentagon ceremony five years after the deadly attack.

A man convicted of providing material support to the Islamic State terror group in connection with the deadly Abbey Gate bombing that killed 13 American service members during the Biden administration's chaotic withdrawal from Afghanistan has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Mohammed Sharifullah, an alleged militant with ISIS-K, a regional branch of the terrorist group, was convicted in April of a conspiracy charge in a deadly 2021 suicide bombing at the Hamid Karzai International Airport in Kabul.

"Sharifullah spent nearly a decade at the heart of a horrific campaign of terror, providing critical support for attacks against civilians around the world and, ultimately, contributed to the deaths of 13 U.S. servicemembers and dozens of others at Abbey Gate," said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John Eisenberg. "Today’s sentence holds him accountable for the blood on his hands. The United States will pursue, capture, and bring to justice anyone, anywhere in the world, who takes part in the killing of our servicemembers or citizens."

During his trial, jurors deadlocked on whether any deaths at the airport "resulted from" that conspiracy. Sharifullah could have faced a possible life sentence if the jury had unanimously agreed on that point.
AFGHAN MAN CONVICTED OF CONSPIRACY IN DEADLY SUICIDE BOMBING AT KABUL AIRPORT DURING US WITHDRAWAL

Inside Abbey Gate, British and American security forces maintain order amongst the Afghan evacuees waiting to leave, in Kabul, Aug. 25, 2021. Mohammed Sharifullah, who was convicted of providing material support to the Islamic State, was sentenced to 20 years in prison in relation to the deadly Abbey Gate suicide bombing during the 2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan. (Marcus Lam/Los Angeles Times/Getty Images)

More than 160 Afghans and 13 U.S. military service members were killed on Aug. 26, 2021, at the airport, where U.S. troops were conducting evacuation operations when a lone suicide bomber detonated an improvised explosive device near Abbey Gate, an entry point.
The U.S. withdrawal was completed days later as the Taliban retook control of the country.

Mark Schmitz, the father of Marine Lance Cpl. Jared Schmitz, who was killed in the bombing, told Fox News that the 20-year sentence is "certainly not enough time for somebody who was involved in something as heinous as this."
"The terrorist bombing took my son physically from me. They can never take his legacy as a human being," he said.
U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said law enforcement remained "steadfast in pursuing" Sharifullah and bringing him to justice on American soil.
"Our hearts remain with the families who lost loved ones that day," Blanche wrote on X. "No sentence can undo their unimaginable loss, but we hope today brings some measure of justice."
PENTAGON CRACKS OPEN BIDEN’S BOTCHED AFGHAN WITHDRAWAL AS SWEEPING REPORT READIES ALL THE RECEIPTS

Afghans hold documents and wait outside Abbey Gate at Hamid Karzai International Airport in Kabul during the chaotic 2021 U.S. evacuation. Many Afghan Christians and allies were among those seeking rescue. (Courtesy: Oklahoma Khorasan Church)

During interviews with the FBI, Sharifullah admitted that he surveilled a possible route for the suicide bomber to the Abbey Gate during the last days of the U.S. military’s presence in Afghanistan, according to evidence presented at trial.

"ISIS-K members provided Sharifullah with a motorcycle, funds for a cell phone and a SIM card, and instructions to open an account on a particular social media platform to communicate with them during the attack operation," an affidavit cited Sharifullah as saying in an FBI interview.
NAVY VETERAN AMONG TRIO WHO ALLEGEDLY WANTED TO BEHEAD SOLDIER AND FUND ISIS DRONE ATTACKS ON AMERICANS

President Donald Trump, surrounded by family members of military service members killed in Afghanistan at the attack at Abbey Gate, speaks during an event for the signing of a proclamation honoring the fourth anniversary of the attack. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

"After making these preparations for the attack, Sharifullah was tasked with scouting a route near Hamid Karzai International Airport for an attacker," the affidavit said. "Sharifullah conducted surveillance on a route, specifically checking for law enforcement and American or Taliban checkpoints."
Prosecutors also presented evidence of several other ISIS-K attacks in Afghanistan in which Sharifullah admitted involvement.
TRUMP’S COUNTERTERRORISM STRATEGY SCORES BIG WINS AGAINST GLOBAL TERROR THREATS
President Donald Trump announced the capture of Sharifullah during a March 2025 address to a joint session of Congress.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Tonight, I am pleased to announce that we have just apprehended the top terrorist responsible for that atrocity. And he is right now on his way here to face the swift sword of American justice," Trump said at the time to lawmakers.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the Justice Department for comment.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Injured Louisiana boy hailed a 'superhero' for seeking help during deadly stabbing rampage
summary: A 6-year-old Houma, Louisiana, boy fled to a neighbor's door after a mass stabbing that killed four Verret family members before passing out inside.
story: "Look, Landry said it tongue in cheek, but there's always a little bit of truth to saying something like that, tongue in cheek. If there were no concerns, it wouldn't be said

A 6-year-old boy from Houma, Louisiana, is being hailed as a "superhero" for escaping a mass stabbing that left four dead, making it to a neighbor's doorstep and passing out inside the house after suffering stab wounds that landed him in the hospital.

The suspect, Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, reportedly followed the boy to the neighbor's door, knocked him to the ground and then fled. Once the boy got into the house, he lost consciousness, according to local WWL, and the neighbor called 911.

Solet was also hospitalized for injuries that took place during the alleged mass stabbing. He was released from the hospital on Tuesday and booked on four counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted first-degree murder, according to the Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office.
MAN ACCUSED IN BRUTAL MOTEL STABBING SOUGHT AS PERSON OF INTEREST IN 4 DEATHS, CHILD ATTACK

Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, was charged with four counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted first-degree murder, according to the Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office. (Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office/Houma Police Department/Google Maps)
The boy is "stable" after suffering multiple stab wounds, his father wrote Tuesday in a Facebook post.
"Please pray for my little man as he recovers he’s so so strong and such a fighter," the father wrote. "Current status (he’s stable) thank everybody for reaching out."

"I just wanna thank everybody for the prayers I’m trying to tell everyone thank you it’s just a lot right now," the boy's father wrote on X, sharing memorials that describe her son as a "superhero" and mourn the loss of four family members, adding his son "appreciates every last one of you reaching out and helping and praying."
DAYCARE OPERATOR ARRESTED AFTER 3-YEAR-OLD WAS LEFT UNCONSCIOUS IN POOL FOR 20 MINUTES, DIED
The Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office took Kaegan Jude Solet into custody after he was hospitalized for his own injuries from the alleged massacre. (Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office)
"I told him earlier that he has so many people behind him and praying for him and he smiled thank yall fr , god bless."
The Terrebonne Sheriff's Office captured Solet early Sunday morning after a manhunt aided by the boy and the neighbor.

"On September 12, 2026, Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office Deputies responded to the 200 block of Ashland Drive, where they located a juvenile suffering from apparent stab wounds," a sheriff's office Facebook post read. "The juvenile was transported by Acadian Ambulance Service Air Med to an out-of-area hospital in critical condition.

"As Deputies continued their preliminary investigation, four deceased victims were discovered inside two nearby residences. Detectives were called in to assist, and began processing multiple scenes, gathering evidence, interviewing witnesses, and developing information surrounding the incidents. During the investigation, Detectives identified Solet as a person of interest and began an intensive effort to locate him."

There was a GoFundMe set up for the boy and his family. The crowdfunding page identified the boy's relatives Verna Mae Verdin and Letha Verret as victims who were killed in their home during the attack. That page had reached almost $60,000 of the $70,000 goal as of Wednesday morning.

"Despite his injuries, he was able to escape and get help," organizer Brandon Thiel said of the 6-year-old survivor. "He is currently in critical condition at a local hospital, where he continues to fight for his life. This devastating tragedy has left the Verret family facing an unimaginable amount of grief, uncertainty, and hardship. The loss is especially profound for Letha’s minor children, who are now having to cope with the sudden loss of their mother, grandmother, and uncle all at once."
ICE BOSTON ARRESTS BRAZILIAN ILLEGAL ALIEN WANTED FOR MURDER DAYS BEFORE GOV HEALY SIGNED PROTECT ACT
Authorities are searching for Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, after identifying him as a person of interest in a series of deadly stabbing incidents. (Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office)
Solet reportedly was known to the family, and the sheriff's reports shared no motive.

"Our hearts remain with the victims, their families and every member of our community who has been affected by this unimaginable tragedy," Sheriff Tim Soignet wrote in a statement posted to Facebook. "We recognize that no words can lessen the pain these families are experiencing, but we want them to know that they are not alone and that our agency remains firmly committed to pursuing justice on their behalf.

"I am incredibly proud of our personnel and supporting agencies whose immediate response and tireless work brought this investigation to this point. Our Deputies are members of this community, and they carry the weight of these tragedies alongside the families and citizens we serve."
The latest investigation is not the first time Solet’s name has surfaced in violent crime allegations.
Solet was arrested in December 2019 for allegedly stabbing a woman repeatedly and leaving her locked inside a Houma motel room, according to a police news release from the time.
Asked why Solet was no longer in custody, Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office Lt. Blake Tabor said authorities were also searching for answers.
"I can’t tell you. Certainly, that’s the hot question, right? Why is he out?" Tabor said. "We’re probably just as stunned as everyone else is."
Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, was allegedly involved in a prior stabbing of an older woman in 2019. (Houma Police Department)

Tabor emphasized that the sheriff’s office has a strong working relationship with the Terrebonne Parish District Attorney’s Office but said questions remain about how Solet’s previous cases were handled.
Deputies found four people dead inside homes near Ashland Drive after responding to a critically wounded child, authorities said. (Google Maps)

"How this slipped through, I certainly don’t know, but it’s a question that probably needs to be answered," Tabor said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the district attorney’s office seeking the circumstances surrounding Solet’s release and whether he remained under any court-ordered supervision but did not immediately receive a response.

title: Erdogan's Turkey cracks down on LGBT community in name of preserving family values
summary: Turkey reportedly arrested some 116 people and blocked 180 social media accounts in a sweeping crackdown on LGBT rights organizations across 15 provinces.
story: FDD Senior fellow Sinan Ciddi explains why he believes Ankara’s policies are reshaping how terrorism is defined and raising concerns inside NATO.

Turkish authorities launched an unprecedented crackdown on the country’s LGBT community on Sunday, raiding gay bars and shutting down activist organizations, in what the government said are efforts to protect Turkey’s family values.

Since the nationwide crackdowns began, Turkish authorities have arrested and detained some 116 people across 15 provinces in actions against LGBT rights organizations and activists. The Turkish criminal justice system has also launched investigations of more than 160 people, according to Amnesty International.
Amnesty International reported that 180 social media accounts belonging to LGBT organizations, activists, journalists and media outlets have been blocked or restricted.
TURKEY’S NATO ROLE UNDER SCRUTINY AMID NEW REPORT ON HAMAS, MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD TIES

Turkish police detain dozens of LGBT rights protesters in Ankara, on September 15, 2026. The arrests interrupted a planned pro-LGBT demonstration in the capital a day after detentions of LGBT activists, media organizations, civil society groups and public figures across Turkey.  (Diego Cupolo/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"This appalling escalation in Türkiye’s crackdown amounts to a full-scale assault on LGBTI rights and those who defend them. The relentless raids, arrests and demonization of LGBTI people under the spurious guise of ‘protecting the families’ demonstrates why defending LGBTI rights in Türkiye is more important than ever," Esther Major, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for Europe, said in a statement.

Turkish police detain dozens of LGBT rights protesters in Ankara, on September 15, 2026. The arrests interrupted a planned pro-LGBT demonstration in the capital a day after detentions of LGBT activists, media organizations, civil society groups and public figures across Turkey. (Diego Cupolo/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

In a statement posted on X, Turkey’s Minister of Justice, Akın Gürlek, said, "we are steadfastly continuing our efforts to protect the family, our children and our youth from all forms of exploitation, obscenity, crime and harmful content."

Gürlek stated that the Ministry of Justice sent a comprehensive directive to the 175 chief public prosecutor's offices in all of Turkey’s 81 provinces to go after content and behavior that the government considers opposed to "public morality" and harmful to the country’s youth.

"The best interests of our children are not open to debate for us. We will show no tolerance for any criminal organization targeting the institution of the family, the future of our youth, and the order of our society," Gürlek’s statement went on to say.
WHO IS TURKEY'S RECEP TAYYIP ERDOĞAN? HOW NATO'S MOST UNPREDICTABLE LEADER KEEPS REINVENTING HIMSELF

Turkey’s focus on family values and traditional norms is part of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s Decade of Family and Population vision, a long-term strategy aimed at tracking population trends and promote an increased fertility rate to spur population growth.
Many see Erdoğan’s renewed emphasis on "family values" and his targeting of groups he portrays as threats to those values as as an effort to cement his legacy.
An enduring question asked by analysts is as Erdogan ages and approaches another election in 2028 is what kind of Turkey he leaves behind.

- Russia's President Vladimir Putin meets with Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in Kazan on October 23, 2024. (ALEXANDER ZEMLIANICHENKO/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

"Erdoğan’s "family values" agenda is about more than defending conservative values, it is about defining what kind of society Turkey should be and who belongs in it," Gonul Tol, senior fellow at the Middle East Institute, told Fox News Digital.

"The LGBT community is a particularly useful target because Erdoğan can portray it simultaneously as a threat to the traditional family, a Western import, and a symbol of the cultural values he says his movement is fighting against," Gonul added.
With protests against the moves beginning to take shape, the crackdowns show no signs of letting up, even as international attention and condemnation begins to pour in.
TRUMP BETS ON FORMER NATO TROUBLEMAKER AS TURKEY'S STRATEGIC VALUE SURGES
Police used pepper spray against peaceful protesters in İzmir, along Turkey’s Aegean coast, and detained more than 95 people on Tuesday who had gathered outside İstanbul Courthouse in protest.
Turkey, which officially became a candidate for the European Union in 1999, received strong pushback from the commission.

Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan speaks during a rally in solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza, amid the ongoing conflict between Israel and the Palestinian Islamist group Hamas, in Istanbul, Turkey October 28, 2023. (Dilara Senkaya/Reuters)

A European Commission spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "The Commission is concerned about the recent arrests and legal proceedings initiated against LGBTIQ+ activists, human rights associations, and businesses, as well as of the blockages of websites and social media accounts, accompanied with allegations concerning funding of civil society organizations. We are following developments closely."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The Commission reiterated that Turkey, as an EU candidate and member of the Council of Europe, should promote and ensure respect for the human rights and dignity of all individuals, regardless of gender or sexual identity.
A spokesman for the Turkish embassy in Washington, D.C., did not respond to requests for comment from Fox News Digital.

title: Fresh activity emerges at Iran’s deeply buried nuclear site as Trump warns Iran not to ‘get cute’
summary: Satellite imagery reveals Iran added new defenses at Pickaxe Mountain near Natanz as Trump warns Tehran not to "get cute" with the nuclear site.
story: FDD’s Behnam Ben Taleblu says Iran’s deeply buried nuclear-linked site poses a growing military challenge as Tehran hardens entrances and rebuilds sensitive facilities.

New satellite imagery shows Iran has added new defenses around tunnel entrances at Pickaxe Mountain, the deeply buried nuclear-linked site President Donald Trump has repeatedly threatened to strike, as Russia and China on Thursday vetoed a U.S.-drafted Security Council resolution aimed at preserving international monitoring of sanctions on Tehran.

The Institute for Science and International Security said in a report released Thursday that satellite imagery from Sept. 11 shows earthen roadblocks remain in place on roads leading to Pickaxe Mountain’s western tunnel portals near the Natanz nuclear complex. The institute said the continued restricted access reinforces its assessment that the facility is not currently being used for normal operations, while assessing that valuable equipment or materials remain inside.

The report also identified additional soil placed over one western tunnel portal and over a nearby cluster of entrances first built in 2007. The institute said the added soil increases the amount of earth protecting the entrances and helps harden them against aerial bombardment.
EXPERTS ‘DEEPLY’ CONCERNED OVER IRAN’S WORK AT UNDERGROUND NUCLEAR SITE
An overview of Iran’s Natanz nuclear complex and nearby Pickaxe Mountain, seen in satellite imagery from Aug. 21, 2026. (Satellite image ©2026 Vantor Technologies.)
The findings come one week after Trump issued his latest warning over Pickaxe Mountain.
"We notice there’s a little activity at Pickaxe," Trump told reporters last week. "I would advise Iran not to get cute because we will have to hit them very hard."

Trump has repeatedly raised the possibility of attacking the site. In a July 28 "Fox & Friends" interview highlighted by the White House, Trump said the U.S. was watching Pickaxe closely and knew "exactly what’s going on," adding that Washington could "take out Pickaxe" if diplomacy failed.

Pickaxe Mountain lies roughly two kilometers from Natanz and features multiple tunnel entrances leading into a deeply buried underground complex. Construction began in 2020 following sabotage that damaged an advanced centrifuge assembly facility at Natanz, and Iranian officials subsequently said a replacement underground facility was being built for advanced centrifuge production. Analysts estimate portions of the facility may be buried at least 100 meters beneath the mountain. Iran has said there is no nuclear activity at the site.
TRUMP SAYS US HAS 'MASSIVE' MUNITIONS STOCKPILE, VOWS 'TREASONOUS' LEAKERS BEING HUNTED DOWN
A closer view of tunnel entrances at Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain, near the Natanz nuclear complex, seen in satellite imagery from Aug. 21, 2026. (Satellite image ©2026 Vantor Technologies)

Behnam Ben Taleblu, senior director of the Iran program at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital that some analysts believe the opportunity for a straightforward strike on Pickaxe Mountain may already have passed.

"The window to strike Pickaxe Mountain, according to some, has already expired because the regime has dug an underground nuclear facility several times deeper than Fordow," Ben Taleblu said. But he argued that Washington retains military options even if destroying the underground complex itself proves difficult.

"Washington can do what it’s traditionally been able to do with sites that are underground, hardened and fortified, and that’s to bury their entrances and raise the political cost to the Islamic Republic of being able to dig out," he said.

"While there may not be the perfect munition just yet, Uncle Sam always has a bigger bomb," Ben Taleblu added. "And in the meantime, what they can do is show that they mean business by burying the entrances."
NUCLEAR EXPERTS URGE TRUMP NOT TO LET IRAN STEER TALKS AWAY FROM REGIME'S ATOMIC THREAT
A satellite view shows an overview of the Natanz nuclear facility and Pickaxe Mountain, near Natanz, Iran, June 30, 2026 (Vantor/Handout via Reuters)
The Pickaxe findings came alongside signs of reconstruction at another sensitive Iranian facility.

In a separate report Thursday, the institute said Iran was "rapidly moving forward" with reconstruction of Taleghan 2 at the Parchin military complex southeast of Tehran. Vantor Technologies satellite imagery from Sept. 13 shows Iran erected a tarp over the destroyed hardened facility, obscuring work underneath from satellite or aerial observation, while dump trucks, bulldozers, concrete equipment and cranes were active around the site.

The institute said Iran also built new concrete reinforcement that could provide additional protection against aerial attack. Taleghan 2 was struck by Israel in October 2024 and again in March 2026 after Iran had rebuilt and hardened the facility. The institute said significant questions remain about Tehran’s plans for the site.
The military developments unfolded alongside a separate confrontation over Iran at the United Nations.
CHINA ORDERS FIRMS TO IGNORE US IRAN SANCTIONS, DARING US TO ENFORCE CRACKDOWN

Satellite imagery shows the underlying structure of the rebuilt Taleghan 2 facility at Iran’s Parchin military complex encased within a concrete "sarcophagus," prior to being covered with soil in Feb. 13, 2026. (Vantor Technologies with annotations by ISIS)

Russia and China on Thursday vetoed a U.S.-authored Security Council resolution that would have extended for another year, until September 2027, the mandate of the Panel of Experts supporting the 1737 Iran Sanctions Committee. The measure received 11 votes in favor, while Pakistan and Somalia abstained.

The panel investigates alleged sanctions violations and reports on implementation. The dispute reflects a deeper split over whether UN sanctions suspended under the 2015 nuclear agreement were legally restored through the "snapback" mechanism. Most Council members maintain that the sanctions and related monitoring structures were revived, while Russia and China reject the legal and procedural validity of that position.
A day before the vote, U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz told reporters in New York that Washington considers the sanctions legally restored.

"The snapback sanctions… occurred, the United States and this U.N. Security Council followed appropriate procedures for that to occur," Waltz said Wednesday at a news conference attended by Fox News Digital. "Those sanctions are in place and we expect those who are a party to fully enforce those sanctions."
Waltz said the expert panel is important because sanctioned companies and individuals can attempt to evade restrictions by changing names and corporate structures.
"The president has been clear, and the world community has been clear with resolution after resolution, that the Iranian regime cannot have a nuclear weapon," Waltz said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Imagery shows Iranian military facility being buried and fortified. (Images via Vantor with annotations from ISIS)

Thursday also brought fresh U.N. scrutiny of both Washington and Tehran. An independent U.N. fact-finding mission said it had reasonable grounds to believe two U.S. strikes on civilian sites in Iran in February constituted war crimes, while separately concluding that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during their crackdown on anti-government protests. The mission is investigative rather than judicial, and its findings do not themselves constitute criminal judgments.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Iran U.N. mission for comments but didn’t receive them in time for publication.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition.
