Who Is At the Top of the Leaderboard?
After the first night, Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson landed at the top of the leaderboard. The two received 7s from each judge for a total of 21 out of 30.
The two celebrated their achievement, especially Shum who shared in his rehearsal video that he was worried about being a great partner.
Was There An Elimination?
Yes, at the end of the episode one couple was eliminated.
After only getting the chance to perform once, Conner Leavitt and partner Adele Zaikman took their last bow.
“This has been the most fun. I have the greatest dance partner in the world in Adele. I can’t wait for the world to see her talent,” Leavitt said after they were eliminated.
On Wednesday, Sept. 16, the ladies will get a chance to show off their moves. The judges’ scores will be combined with the live viewer votes to determine which couple will also be eliminated.
How to Vote for the ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Contestants
Usually, fans will be able to vote for their favorite couple during the live simulcast of the show in the ET/CT time zones by heading to the “Dancing With the Stars” website.
However, during the Sept. 15 broadcast co-host Julianne Hough informed viewers online voting was down and that audiences needed to vote via text. Votes through the website did not count.
Throughout the season, U.S. viewers can vote by SMS/text message during the live voting window each episode/week. Voting by text cannot be changed and only the first 10 count.
If voting online, viewers get up to 10 votes and can change and save their votes throughout the telecast.
Voting is only open at this time for the male celebrities who performed on Sept. 15. Tomorrow, during the live telecast, viewers can vote for the female celebrities competing.

title: Does Taylor Swift’s ‘SVU’ Skit Have a Secret Message to Her Fans?
summary: What could “saccharide, Aries, from the vineyard, north or south” really mean? Taylor Swift’s “SVU” skit at the Emmys has her fans speculating about Easter Eggs.
story: “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.”

These arbitrary phrases have left Swifties everywhere with dozens of questions after the Emmy Awards, the main one being: Is Taylor Swift the mastermind her fans know her to be, or did she just send them on a wild goose chase?

Clues point to the former. But first, let’s rewind for those who need it: Mariska Hargitay had hosted the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards on Sept. 14 and had tapped Swift, her friend and longtime “Law & Order: SVU” fan, to appear in an “SVU” parody skit that aired during the telecast.
The pre-taped sketch features Hargitay, Ice-T, Kelli Giddish, Peter Scanavino and more actors playing their characters from the crime drama. Their case to crack: Will Taylor Swift attend the Emmys?

Hargitay, as Olivia Benson, brought up as evidence Swift’s love of Easter eggs. She wheeled out a crime board filled with clues as each person took turns suggesting why certain nominees and shows pointed toward Swift making a surprise appearance.
Suddenly, a crime board was wheeled away to reveal Swift was standing in the precinct.
“Hey guys, this isn’t adding up,” she said while wearing a gray suit and holding a coffee mug.
Ice-T rebuffed her input. “And who asked you, rookie?” he said.
She replied, “Our perp has a clear M.O. A lot of this doesn’t fit the pattern, and I don’t think everything is a clue.”
“It is to the Swifties,” Hargitay quickly replied.
“I think what we’re going to be looking for is hiding in plain sight,” Swift replied.
She then panned and spoke directly to the camera: “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.”
“What did you just say?” Hargitay asked her.
“I didn’t say anything,” Swift said with a shrug.

While the sketch wraps by cracking its case — Swift won’t be at the Emmys because she’ll be busy supporting husband Travis Kelce at the Chiefs season opener — the meaning of Swift’s spoken message is still a mystery.
Swifties of course know that nothing is ever that simple when it comes to the singer. They immediately began dissecting the skit on social media, seeing if they could decode a secret message.
What could it mean? Well, the Emmys executive producers have confirmed that the words have some type of significance because they were specifically chosen by Swift.

After the Emmys, executive producers Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzon-Clay from Jesse Collins Entertainment, and NBCUniversal live events and specials exec VP Jen Neal, spoke with reporters and explained how they pulled off the sketch.
“Taylor loved the script and she had some thoughts and we worked that in,” Collins told reporters, according to Variety.
One of Swift’s notes was to add Easter eggs, Collins revealed.
“She wanted them to be really official. And correct,” Rouzan-Clay shared.

As always, Swifties are on the case, and they might’ve already cracked it. Many shared their theories on social media that the sketch pointed to Swift releasing the long-awaited “Taylor’s Versions” from her debut and “Reputation” albums.
One Swiftie said on X that Ice-T’s “rookie” line and Aries, the first astrological sign, reference her self-titled first album.

Another zoomed in on the crime board and noticed a Post-it note that read “Is it TV?” adding more fuel to the fire. The board also had a heart similar to the one Swift used to draw on the back of her hand during the early days of her career.
Beneath the post, one X user replied, “Olivia said ‘the answer has been TV this whole time’ also.”
But others were more convinced that “Reputation (Taylor’s Version)” is on the way.

“I believe Debut TV is next but to add fuel to the Rep TV fire (no pun intended), if you go all the way back to the Karma MV in the Reputation scene Taylor wears the ram mask and the ram is the Aries zodiac animal,” one tweeted.
Over on Reddit, the speculation continued.
“I’m putting in my guess now — these are Rep vault track titles,” one suggested.
And one fan had a wild but plausible idea.
“OMG GUYS THERES TWO BOARDS!!! TWO!!” they said. “We are getting both Debut and Rep.”
Looks like we’ll have to wait for Swift’s next message to see what other tricks she has up her sleeve.

title: All About Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys’ Relationship, From How They Met to ‘The Americans’
summary: On screen, Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys paired a pair of married Russian spies living undercover in “The Americans,” which ran from 2013 to 2018 on FX.
story: On screen, Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys paired a pair of married Russian spies living undercover in “The Americans,” which ran from 2013 to 2018 on FX.
Off screen, the “Felicity” star and the Welsh actor were falling in love.

While “The Americans” was still airing in 2017, the couple spoke to People about making their relationship work. Russell said a bit of “alone time,” since they spend so much time together. Plus, Rhys said, “she has the patience of a saint, so that helps.”
Rhys and Russell turned heads at the 2026 Emmys, where they appeared on the red carpet together because they were both nominated for acting awards.

Russell was nominated for outstanding lead actress in a drama series for her role as Kate Wyler in “The Diplomat,” which she lost, and Rhys was nominated — and won — for both outstanding lead actor in a comedy series as Tom Loftis in “Widow’s Bay” and outstanding lead actor in a limited or anthology series or movie as Nile Jarvis in “The Beast in Me.”

But when the trophies where handed out, Rhys still felt that Russell came out on top. In a video captured by the Associated Press, he praised his longtime partner for her more measured approach to awards season: After joking that he tends to brag about his wins more than Russell, who is always supportive of her competitors, Rhys quipped, “She’s always really the winner, if I’m perfectly honest.”
Here’s what to know about their roughly 13-year-long relationship.
They Met Long Before “The Americans”
During a joint appearance on “Watch What Happens Live“ in 2017, Rhys and Russell recalled the first time they met.
Rhys said it was a “a very long, long time ago” — back when he was 26 years old.
“I very drunkenly asked her for her number when she was a young single slip of a thing,” Rhys said.
They had met after a “kickball party,” Russell said. The conversation happened in a parking lot after Russell asked Rhys to open up a beer for her.
Rhys gave more of the story in a 2023 appearance on “Watch What Happens Live.” He left her a drunken voice mail — to which she didn’t respond.
Their Romance Rekindled on ‘The Americans’
But “it took a while,” Rhys said of their love story on “Watch What Happens Live.”
Russell said that one day, after a “heavy dose of fight training,” Rhys told her, “We’ve met before.”
She responded, “No, we haven’t.” Rhys then reminded her about the “drunken message” he left her. “As soon as he said that, I knew exactly what he meant,” she said.
Russell said in a later interview with Variety in 2024 that they fell in love shooting the first season.
“I was in love with Matthew,” Russell said. “We were, like, hot and heavy in love, shooting the spy stuff at night in disguises and wigs. I mean, it was such a fun, sexy time. So fun, oh my gosh.”
They Kept Their Romance a Secret On Set
Rhys told Andy Cohen in a 2023 appearance on “Watch What Happens Live” that he and Russell kept their relationship private on set for “about a year.”
Rhys told People how they broke the news to their producers — not only that they were dating, but that they were expecting a baby. Their son, Sam, was born between Seasons 4 and 5.

“So when we told our producers like, ‘Oh, we do have something to say,’ they’re like, ‘Oh, don’t tell us you’re together.’ We’re like, ‘Actually, we’re going to have a baby.’ They were like, ‘Oh my God,’ because we’d kept it a secret for so long.”
Their Son, Sam, Was Born in 2016
Rhys and Russell welcomed their son, Sam, into the world in 2016. That year, Russell raved about their kid in an interview with TODAY. She said, “He’s so good. He’s big and fat and nice.”
Russell is also mom to two kids, River and Willa, from her marriage to her ex-husband, carpenter Shane Deary.
They’re Not Married — But Matthew Rhys Joked About Proposing in an Acceptance Speech

At the 2018 Emmys, Rhys won the award for outstanding lead actor in a drama series for his role in “The Americans.” When he was announced as the winner, the actor gave Russell a big kiss on before making his way to the stage.
Near the end of his acceptance speech, he peered out into the audience and thanked Russell.

“And finally, to the woman who truly got me this award, who just stands in front of me every day and just puts up with me. She said, ‘If you propose to me, I would punch you clean in the mouth.’ I don’t have the words or the time, neither which would do you justice, Keri Lynn, except thank you, more to come, thank you.”
They Were Both Nominated Multiple Times for ‘The Americans’
Keri Russell was up for an Emmy in 2016, 2017 and 2018 for “The Americans.” Rhys was nominated the same years but won in 2018.
When they were both up for Golden Globes for “The Americans” in 2019, the couple joked about their coordinated awards in an interview with with Ryan Seacrest for E! News.
“Thank God we don’t have to break up,” Russell joked.
They Recently Reunited on Screen for ‘Cocaine Bear’
In 2018, “The Americans” aired its final episode. They reunited on screen for the 2023 flick “Cocaine Bear.”

“I unashamedly jumped on my partner’s coattails because I knew (Keri Russell) was doing this movie with (director) Elizabeth Banks, who we know, and I read the script and I simply said, ‘Who’s playing that? That little fun part, a few seconds in the beginning?’ She goes, ‘I don’t know.’ I said, ‘Ask Banks.’ And then she said, ‘No, it’s been cast,’ and I said ‘Tell Banks I’ll do it.’ And then I was like, ‘Well actually, just ask her if I can do it,’” Rhys told The A.V. Club.
Rhys Supports Russell in Her ‘Diplomat’ Era
Rhys and Russell walked the red carpet together at the 2024 Golden Globes. That year, Russell was nominated for an Emmy for the Netflix drama “The Diplomat.” She’s up for an award again this year.
In an interview with Variety about her work in “The Diplomat,” Rhys gave an assessment of his partner’s personality.

“She is naturally a very shy person, and to expose herself in that way day after day, I think she finds both taxing and challenging. But she is a mind, and she loves being challenged, and she loves words — books are her biggest passion. Words and narrative are her great love.”

title: It’s the Great Pumpkin (Spice Latte), Charlie Brown: Starbucks Launches Peanuts Collection
summary: This pumpkin spice season, Starbucks is rolling out the limited-edition Peanuts + Starbucks collection items featuring a Snoopy glass cold cup.
story: The Peanuts gang is celebrating the arrival of the Great Pumpkin ... Spice Latte.

Starbucks is marking the return of everything pumpkin spice this fall by rolling out 10 collectible items featuring Snoopy, Charlie Brown and company as part of its limited-edition Peanuts + Starbucks collection.

Starbucks locations around the world will be selling the collectibles while supplies last. The collection coincides with the 60th anniversary of the classic, Halloween-themed Peanuts show “It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown.”

The headliner is a Snoopy glass cold cup with the iconic “Peanuts” character wearing a winter hat and orange beanie with his pal Woodstock perched on the top of the straw. The Snoopy glass follows the viral Starbucks Bearista cup, which caused a frenzy in 2025, was dressed up for the World Cup in July and turned pink in a separate promotion.
Here’s what to know about the Peanuts + Starbucks collection, as well as the two limited-edition, Peanuts-themed beverages that Starbucks is selling.

title: All 13 of Mariska Hargitay’s Emmys Looks — Including 1 That Honors Mom Jayne Mansfield
summary: Take a look at all of the outfits Mariska Hargitay wore as she hosted the Emmy Awards.
story: When someone says Mariska Hargitay is the hostess with the mostest, they may be referring to the number of outfits she wore.

The “Law & Order: SVU” star hosted the Emmy Awards for the first time on Sept. 14 and proceeded to wear at least 13 different outfits during the evening — and that doesn’t include what she sported in her pre-taped sketch with Taylor Swift.

Hargitay first walked the red carpet in a flowing red sequined gown with one strap hanging off her shoulder. It matched a red sparkly dress worn by her daughter, Amaya, 15, for the occasion. The Emmys carpet was a true family affair for Hargitay, who was also joined by husband Peter Hermann and their sons August, 20, and Andrew, 14.

Many fans pointed out that Hargitay and Amaya’s red dresses seemingly re-created a red dress the Emmy host’s mother, Jayne Mansfield, wore in the 1956 musical, “The Girl Can’t Help It.” Before her hosting gig, Hargitay won two Emmys for her HBO documentary “My Mom Jayne.”
But Hargitay latest homage to her mom’s fashion was merely the beginning of her cavalcade of costumes, as she slipped into a shimmering, strapless off-white dress to deliver her opening monologue.

To open the show, she joked about the audience being full of former “SVU” guest stars, celebrated her status as the first female host in 15 years, and re-created Nicole Kidman’s famous AMC ad to honor TV storytelling.
Throughout the night, Hargitay made frequent costume changes, including a sleek black gown with matching gloves, a satin white suit and a fur-lined cape paired with a sword.
Take a look at some of Hargitay’s fashion highlights worn over the course of the evening:
As the evening wound down, Hargitay said she enjoyed the experience.
“It’s been an absolute delight to be your host,” she said as the show drew to a close. “Thank you for all the love and joy tonight.
“And now that we’ve reached the end, there’s only one thing left to do,” she said as the iconic “dun, dun” from “Law & Order: SVU” played.
“God, I love it when it does that!”

title: Yes, Witney Carson Is Pregnant. And Yes, She Will Still Be Competing on ‘DWTS’: ‘It’s a Big Blessing to Do Both’
summary: On Aug. 17, “Dancing With the Stars” announced that pro dancer Witney Carson would be paired with Guillermo Rodriguez for Season 35.
story: On Aug. 17, “Dancing With the Stars” announced that pro dancer Witney Carson would be paired with Guillermo Rodriguez for Season 35. That same day, she revealed she was pregnant with her third child.

The announcement had many people wondering how she would be able to compete since the new season didn’t start for another month. But as Carson tells TODAY.com, she and husband Carson McAllister were set on expanding their family, and she didn’t think she needed to put her career on hold.

“We decided we wanted to grow our family. It’s time,” Carson, mom to sons Kevin, 5, and Jet, 3, says. “We know that we want a lot of kids and we thought it was a perfect year to start doing that. Then this opportunity came up again to do the show, and it just felt like, ‘You know what? I kind of want to prove to myself that I can do both!’ And I love both.”

Dancing since she was a child, Carson first gained fame after competing on Season 9 of “So You Think You Can Dance” in 2012.  The following year, she joined the “DWTS” troupe, before being promoted to a pro for Season 18 in 2014.

“I love to dance, and I love to compete, and I want to grow my family, as well,” the 32-year-old says. “I don’t feel like people necessarily have to lose parts of themselves to keep growing their family. That’s kind of my mantra. I’m gonna stay true to what I love and continue on my career and continue to grow my family. It’s a big blessing to be able to do both.”
For now, Carson is “feeling good,” listening to her body and making sure her baby’s healthy.

“As much as I want to dance and want to do all of it, I really have to be careful to make sure that I don’t overdo it,” she notes. “It’s perfectly safe to do all the things and I’m really not taking this any differently than I would any other season as far as mentally and physically.”

Taking it week by week, among her priorities is making sure she and her growing family are properly fueled. With a jam-packed schedule full of rehearsals and taking care of her boys with another on the way, Carson says she’s grateful for her Campbell’s partnership and the ability to make easy meals for her family.
“I remember my mom always making a hot meal with Campbell’s and so it’s very nostalgic for me,” she says. “It goes back to my childhood.”

Season 35 of “DWTS” kicks off on Sept. 15, which coincides with Campbell’s Two-Step Tuesdays launch celebrating its new sauces. Carson notes that after making a meal with the lemon garlic option, “Everyone gobbled it up ... I love to make dinner. I love doing that for my family. But I don’t have a lot of time, so being able to do something really simple like this two-step dinner is just an absolute dream.”
What is taking more than just two steps is preparing for her and Rodriguez’s competition debut. During the first episode, the duo will perform a cha cha to “Mr. Big Stuff” by Jean Knight.

“I’m really just having fun and Guillermo’s obviously very funny, he’s very heartwarming, he’s adorable,” she says of the “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” star. “He’s already so loved, and honestly, I’m really taking this season no differently than I would any other season. And I think people are a little surprised that you can continue to dance the way that I have.”

Last season, Carson took home her second Mirrorball trophy after coming in first place with Robert Irwin. While many might underestimate her and the comedian’s chances, she could go far depending on votes. (Let’s not forget how Andy Richter was dubbed “the People’s Princess” and made it to the quarterfinals.)

“There’s a TikTok floating around that’s ... not of me, but it’s of a pregnant woman and she’s got a big belly, and she’s break dancing on it,” Carson says. “And the meme is like, ‘Witney, when she makes it to the finale,’ and I’m like, ‘Oh my gosh, literally!’”
With the possibility of her baby being crowned the youngest “DWTS” champ, Carson is ready for this new adventure.
“Listen, I’m prepared for it, kind of,” she says with a laugh. “I’ve never danced this far pregnant ... But listen, I will make it happen. I mean, I’m not injured. I’m just pregnant.”

title: Emily St. John Mandel’s ‘Exit Party’ Envisions Hope in a U.S. Torn Apart by Civil War. Read the First Page
summary: Read the first page of Emily St. John Mandel’s new novel “Exit Party.” The author breaks down the book’s setting and themes.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
Emily St. John Mandel has always been interested in the aftermath of catastrophe.
The acclaimed author of “Station Eleven” doesn’t waste any time getting to that cataclysm on the opening page of her new novel, “Exit Party,” which hits stores on Sept. 15.
“In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace."
Mandel tells TODAY.com she wanted the novel’s very first line to have a “shock effect.”

“I just wanted to avoid confusion and plunge the reader immediately into this world I was creating,” Mandel tells TODAY.com. “It’s a very fast opening. We have the U.S. coming undone in literally the first sentence.”

It’s a theme Mandel has long explored in her work. In her 2014 bestseller “Station Eleven,” a group of survivors try to preserve art and human connection after the world is devastated by a deadly pandemic.
In “Exit Party,” a pair of connected storylines depict an “A side” of America splintered by civil war and a “B side” of a U.S. completely under totalitarian rule.

“I first started writing in the spring of 2022, and it seemed clear to me that I was extrapolating from our current world on the A side, where division turns into conflict,” Mandel says. “But by the time I finished the book about a year ago, I felt like I was struggling to stay ahead of the news cycle on the B side, the authoritarian state. The idea of America where secret police pick people off the street and disappear them felt fictional in 2022.”

“Exit Party” imagines how humans will try to retain connection and resilience in extreme circumstances, whether by throwing parties, putting on plays or performing a concert in a time of war or repression. Mandel says she was inspired by a 2016 story during the civil war in Syria in which residents in the war-torn town of Daraya assembled a secret underground library.
“You just want the characters to find these moments of brightness and ways to feel like you’re doing more than just surviving,” Mandel says.

The novel involves the ongoing journey of Aria, a character from her 2009 novel “The Singer’s Gun,” who has been released after 18 years in prison to an America divided by warring factions in the year 2031. She wanders a fractured Los Angeles, where the fighting has subsided for now.

“I think it’s important to me to try to kind of lean into these times when even though everything is wrong, there are moments that are good,” Mandel says. “This feeling of desperate joy at the end of the world.”
A primary theme of the novel is impermanence. A catastrophe has happened, but the characters work to find their way through to the other side of it.

“This idea that nothing lasts forever, and something always comes next after terrible moments we live through,” Mandel says. “It’s a book about resilience. Can you be resilient in these objectively awful times, because nothing lasts forever. Can you find hope in a state of impermanence?”

For those who enjoyed the Emmy-nominated “Station Eleven” television series in 2021-2022 on HBO Max, “Exit Party” is also being made for television. The feature project was bought by Laika Studios and will be produced by Amy Hodge of Fruit Tree, a film and television production company co-founded by Oscar winner Emma Stone and her husband, Dave McCary.
This time, Mandel, who did not work on the TV adaptation of “Station Eleven,” is adapting “Exit Party” for the screen.

“It’s been a challenge and fun,” she says. “I’ve always enjoyed revision, and for me, adaptation almost feels like a continuation of that. You realize pretty early on that you have to be willing to blow up the book to make it work onscreen.”
Read the First Page of Emily St. John Mandel’s ‘Exit Party’

In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace. The trees bloomed in the same week that international peacekeeping troops withdrew from Los Angeles, and the convergence of flowers with the absence of foreign soldiers brought a delirious kind of hope. Everyone in the spring of 2031 knew the city was one terrorist attack away from disaster, but that peril made the season more vivid, not less.

It was Ari’s first spring outside of prison in nearly two decades, and she spent hours at a time walking the streets. Prison is a wasteland of sensory deprivation, and now the city was overwhelming. She kept expecting that the details of the world would cease to be extraordinary, but that kept not happening. No one around her seemed to notice the jacarandas, because in Los Angeles there are flowers every month of the year, but she walked streets where the trees were lit up by purple-blue blossoms and thought, My god. This place. She was forty-eight years old but felt younger, because so much of the world was new.

The United States had come undone following a coup d’état. Several states had seceded within a week of the coup, either alone or in alliances with neighbors, and war had broken out within the month. Now the fighting had subsided, for the most part, and Ari had been released into an uneasy aftermath.

title: Emmy Winners Full List 2026: Matthew Rhys, Jean Smart Make History as ‘Widow’s Bay’ Sweeps Awards
summary: See a full list of Emmys 2026 winners as the awards are broadcast from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on Monday, Sept. 14.
story: The 78th annual Emmy Awards are officially over. This year, the awards were broadcast from Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on Monday, Sept. 14, and hosted by Mariska Hargitay.

Television fans found out which stars came out victorious in tough categories like outstanding lead actress in a drama series and outstanding lead actor in a comedy series. This year, Zendaya, Jean Smart, Sterling K. Brown, Noah Wyle and more received nominations. There were also 28 actors who received their first-ever Emmy nods.
Follow live coverage of the 2026 Emmys

Two actors in particular made history at the Emmys with their respective wins this year. Jean Smart became the first woman to win an Emmy for every season of a show with her fifth trophy for “Hacks”; and Matthew Rhys became the first person to win two leading acting Emmys for two different series in the same year.
Going into the night, “The Pitt” led the pack with 25 nominations. “Hacks” picked up 24 nods and new series “Widow’s Bay” impressed with 19.

A week before the Sept. 14 ceremony, a number of winners were announced at the Creative Arts Emmys. Hargitay took home two Emmys for her documentary “My Mom Jayne,” while Rob Reiner received a posthumous win for his role on “The Bear.” Bad Bunny, Shailene Woodley, David Harbour and Linda Cardellini were also winners headed into the night.

title: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner Receive Moving Tributes During 2026 Emmys ‘In Memoriam’
summary: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner received tributes at the 2026 Emmy Awards’ “In Memoriam” segment led by performers who were close to each of them.
story: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner received tributes at the 2026 Emmy Awards’ “In Memoriam” segment led by performers who were close to each of them.

O’Hara’s former co-stars — Macaulay Culkin of “Home Alone” and Annie Murphy and Dan Levy of “Schitt’s Creek — celebrated the late actor in an emotional moment that began the segment. To start, Culkin, who as a child actor played O’Hara’s character’s son in the movie franchise, described the special connection the two shared.
Follow live coverage of the 2026 Emmys

“She was encouraging. She was warm. She was funny, but the word that I think of is ‘mama.’ You know, she wasn’t just a wife and mother to Beau and Matthew. She was my mom. She was our mom, and by extension, she’s all of her mom,” Culkin said.
“She may have forgotten me, twice,” Culkin said, poking fun at the movies’ plots, “but we will always remember her.”
Murphy, who with Levy played the adult kids of O’Hara’s character in “Schitt’s Creek,” said O’Hara’s laugh “challenged anyone who heard it to join in and be as delighted as she was.”
Levy said the most important lesson he learned from O’Hara was to “say yes” to new challenges and adventures, including the joyful creation of her quirky bewigged character Moira Rose.

“Say yes to her naming that wig,” Levy said. “Say yes to giving her space to experiment and create. It will amaze you on a daily basis, and it will change your life. Say yes to her dinner invites and her stories and her wisdom and her generosity.”

Later during the “In Memoriam” segment, Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter Noah Kahan performed Simon & Garfunkel’s hit 1970 ballad “Bridge Over Troubled Water” as viewers saw images of other beloved stars who died over the past year, including Dolly Parton, James Van Der Beek, Hayden Panettiere, Eric Dane and more.
On the red carpet before the ceremony, Kahan explained to TODAY’s Sheinelle Jones why he chose to sing “Bridge Over Troubled Water” for Parton and others.
“It’s always represented so much hope and peace and kindness, which I think Dolly personified throughout her life and career,” said Kahan.

“We lost so many legends this year. I am really excited to get the chance to help memorialize them and to pay the respect to those who have contribute to this amazing industry and to art and culture,” added the singer.
The “In Memoriam” segment ended with a tearful Jamie Lee Curtis honoring late creator and director James Burrow and Hollywood director Rob Reiner, who she called a “cherished legend.”
Reiner got his start in television as an actor on “All in the Family” in the 1970s. Curtis described Reiner as “generous and kind and funny as hell and a friend to all.”
Last week, Reiner won a posthumous Emmy for a guest role on “The Bear,” Curtis revealed, breaking a record his father, comedy giant Carl Reiner, had held for longest time in between Emmy wins.
Reiner’s last Emmy award for acting came 48 years ago for “All in the Family.”

title: Reba McEntire Honors Dolly Parton at 2026 Emmys With Touching Cover Performance
summary: Sally Field and Reba McEntire paid a special tribute to their late longtime friend Dolly Parton at the 2026 Emmys.
story: Sally Field and Reba McEntire paid a special tribute to their late longtime friend Dolly Parton at the 2026 Emmys.

“If there are truly angels on earth then we just lost one: Dolly Parton,” said Field, who co-starred alongside Parton, Julia Roberts, Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis and Daryl Hannah in the 1989 comedy “Steel Magnolias.”
“I adored her from day one and how could you not?” said Field. She remembered Parton, who died Aug. 25 at age 80 after a brief cancer battle, as “blisteringly funny.”
“She was genuine and humble and supportive,” Field said before acknowledging Parton’s humanitarianism had “made a profound difference” in the lives of many around the country.
“God bless you, Dolly Parton. I am not the only one on earth who will love you forever and forever,” Field said before footage of Parton appeared onscreen.
McEntire then took the stage to perform Parton’s ballad “Appalachian Memories.”
After Parton’s family announced her death, McEntire was among the first celebrities to pay tribute in an emotional Instagram post.
“There will never ever be another you,” McEntire wrote alongside a gallery of images of the longtime friends. “We will remember and cherish every memory and every note you ever played and sang.”
“She’s gonna have a blast in heaven singing all her favorite songs with all her family and friends who have gone on before her,” she added.
McEntire revealed during a “MasterClass” session on country music that she first met the Queen of Country in September 1977 backstage at the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville.
McEntire, who was scheduled to make her debut at the famed venue that night, learned the performance would be cut short because Parton, already a major star, had shown up unannounced.

“So I walked in, and they said, ‘Reba, I’m terribly sorry, but the two songs that we said you could sing, you’re only going to get to sing one. I said, ‘Why?’ And they said, ‘Well, Dolly Parton just pulled in the parking lot, and she’s going to take one of your songs.”
Rather than feel slighted, McEntire was thrilled.
“I said, ‘OK, can I meet her?!’” she recalled, laughing. “I didn’t care or anything. I just wanted to see Dolly Parton.”
McEntire also recalled seeing Parton for the first time backstage.
“She came walking in and I kind of backed up against the wall, and she had on the most beautiful black chiffon pantsuit with rhinestone butterflies on them and her beautiful hair,” McEntire said.
“I thought, ‘My gosh, that’s probably what an angel looks just like right there.”

title: How Canada and the E.U. are teaming up to counter Trump
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg to lay out how middle powers might counteract Trump’s hostility.
story: Around 3,700 miles separate the Gothic towers of Canada’s Parliament in Ottawa from the glass-fronted modern European Parliament building in eastern France.
But judging by the thunderous applause shaking the E.U. chamber Thursday, President Donald Trump’s threats are helping to close that distance.

Canada and Europe have long been close U.S. allies, benefiting from American military power and trading heft. But Trump has upended those relationships, waging trade wars against Canada and the E.U., while threatening to absorb Canada as America’s 51st state and take control of Greenland, Denmark’s autonomous Arctic territory.
Without a reliable partner in the White House, the spurned allies are now forging their own path.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney urged the world’s “middle powers” to join forces in a speech before the European Parliament in Strasbourg on Thursday to create “an alliance strong enough so that no one can dictate our choices.”
The strategy in short: strength in numbers.
“I’m not proposing a third bloc in order to become a great power rival, only with better manners,” he stressed.

“We do not seek power to dominate others,” Carney continued. “On the contrary, we are pursuing resilience. So no one — no one — can control our open markets, impair our sovereignty, threaten our territorial integrity or undermine our freedoms, our democracies, our rule of law.”

The remarks appeared aimed in part at Trump, though Carney did not name the president in his speech. The response in the room was a near-unanimous standing ovation from lawmakers representing the bloc’s 27 member countries.
Some European leaders, meanwhile, appear ready to grant Canada more favorable access to its closely guarded single market.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen caused a stir Wednesday when she suggested making Canada the E.U.’s first “associate member.” She also outlined an “alliance for the future” that would increase cooperation on defense, energy, critical minerals, artificial intelligence and other tech.
“This is a partnership not against anyone else, but for our common strength,” she said.

At a news conference Thursday, Carney stressed that Canada was “not in a position, nor seeking, to become a full member” of the European Union, a long and drawn-out process of regulatory alignment that can sometimes take decades for applicant countries.
“What matters is the substance,” he said of the associate membership proposal.

Carney has deep links to Europe, having served as governor of the Bank of England before his political homecoming propelled him to Canada’s leadership. He tapped into those ties Wednesday, bonding with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham at an Everton soccer match.

title: Rubio takes behind-the-scenes role on Iran war, while keeping his options open for the future
summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio isn’t the face of the Iran negotiations. He’s kept a discreet public distance as the unpopular war grinds on.
story: WASHINGTON — The talks to end the Iran war had hit a snag.

Vice President JD Vance had flown to Pakistan for negotiations with the Iranians, a sign that the two sides had narrowed their differences and the White House might be poised to announce a breakthrough.

As the marathon April meeting unfolded, though, U.S. negotiators began to worry: It looked like the Iranians were changing the terms of a potential deal. So, during a pause, they phoned Secretary of State Marco Rubio to get a “steer” on what they should do next, an administration official with direct knowledge of the matter said in an interview.
Rubio agreed that they couldn’t accept Iran’s offer, the official said. There would be no deal.

Rubio isn’t the face of the Iran negotiations. He’s kept a discreet public distance as the unpopular war grinds on. Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and the president’s longtime friend and special envoy Steve Witkoff are the main protagonists in the push to end both the Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts.

The arrangement is an unusual one. Past secretaries of state commanded the spotlight when it came to war and peace. Henry Kissinger won a Nobel Peace Prize in 1973 for negotiating a ceasefire in the Vietnam War during the Nixon administration. John Kerry, in the Obama administration, flew back and forth between Washington and the Middle East as he tried in vain to broker a peace deal between the Israelis and Palestinians.
Still, Rubio has been a hidden hand throughout, helping craft the Trump administration’s strategy while privately advising the officials who play a more public role in the peace talks.

He holds a unique place in the Cabinet, one of the most expansive in the modern presidency. Rubio doubles as national security adviser — first in an acting capacity, now permanent — meaning he has a spacious office in the West Wing and gets more face time with Trump than most Cabinet members.

This account is based on interviews with 12 present and former administration officials and others close to Rubio and the White House. Many spoke on condition of anonymity to talk freely about internal policy and political dynamics.

“The reason that the American people perhaps don’t see Secretary Rubio as front and center on Iran is because he really does have the rest of the world to worry about and pays enormous attention to the Western Hemisphere and our European allies,” White House chief of staff Susie Wiles told NBC News. “President Trump is so busy and active around the world, it takes more than one person. So, Secretary Rubio is leading the other efforts around the world that are so important to America’s stability and future promise.”
Add to Google
Add to Google

Trump has given Rubio wide latitude, allowing America’s top diplomat to be selective when it comes to the public parts of the job. Rubio was more visible in the early phase of the Iran war than in the later stages. That could prove advantageous down the road.

Polls show widespread American disenchantment with the conflict. As public opinion hardens, Rubio may be better positioned to sidestep any political backlash than Vance, who has attended futile rounds of peace talks in far-flung locales.

Rubio has said publicly that he currently has no plans to run in 2028, and two people familiar with the matter have told NBC News he has also said that privately. He has acknowledged behind closed doors that the landscape may be tough for Republicans in 2028 and suggested that a presidential run in 2032 or 2036 may be more promising, a person close to him said.
But Rubio’s comments don’t close the door completely. A second person close to him said that he has not ruled out a potential 2028 presidential run, but he is not discussing his future plans.
“Nobody knows what he’s going to do,” the source said. “Political calculation does not factor into literally anything that he’s doing right now.”

Another consideration is personal. Rubio has also said privately that after nearly three decades in public office he may want to take a job in the private sector when Trump’s term ends, two people familiar with the matter told NBC News.

His financial disclosure form shows his net worth to be no more than $240,000 apart from his house, listed in a range between $1 million and $5 million. Those are modest sums in an administration packed with officials worth $100 million or more.
Rubio could readily land a lucrative job that would be a boon to himself, his wife and their four children if he sat out the race, and at 55, he is young enough to mount a campaign later on.
Relationship with Trump

Once angry rivals, Rubio and Trump have developed a good rapport. Rubio may be in and out of the Oval Office five or six times a day, a White House official told NBC News. Both love sports, and they’ve been overheard jawing about baseball batting averages or a knockout punch in the latest mixed martial arts match, the official said.

Olivia Wales, a White House spokesperson, said in a prepared statement: “As President Trump says, Marco Rubio will go down as one of the greatest Secretaries of State in history. The president and Secretary Rubio have successfully restored American dominance on the world stage and are relentlessly working to advance our foreign policy interests.”

After spending 14 years in the Senate, Rubio grasps the politics and legislative tactics needed to pass bills into law and will advise the president on ways to push his agenda through Congress, the official said.

“I can think of many times in which we’re talking about whatever he [Trump] is focused on that day and he’ll say, ‘What do you think, Marco?’ I’ve heard that more times than I can count,” a person close to the White House said. “They jell well together. I’ve seen people who don’t jell well with the president, and Marco is not one of those people.”

Rubio’s influence in the peace talks is largely behind the scenes. Witkoff checks in with him before agreeing to attend negotiating sessions, takes guidance before meetings and briefs him afterward, the administration official said.

Last weekend, the two men spoke by phone multiple times about an escalating conflict involving Iran and Yemen. On Saturday, Witkoff reached Rubio while the secretary of state was at the University of Florida football stadium in Gainesville, watching his son play for the Gators, the official said.

Leaving the Senate last year to work for Trump was a gamble for Rubio. The two faced off in the 2016 Republican presidential primaries, where they one-upped each other in schoolyard taunts. Trump derided the Florida lawmaker as “Little Marco.” Rubio mocked the New York businessman’s hand size.
Time and pragmatic politics have transformed the rivalry into a partnership. The Senate confirmed Rubio by a vote of 99-0, a feat that has impressed even Trump.

“It’s not an easy job to be both the secretary of state and the national security adviser, but Secretary Rubio has managed it beautifully,” Wiles said. “He is an experienced, smart and intuitive adviser to the president and the rest of the team, be it national security or foreign affairs.”
Venezuela and a legacy

Other Cabinet secretaries have flamed out since Trump began his second term. Attorney General Pam Bondi is gone, as are Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer and Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard.

Rubio, by contrast, has thrived in a job that aligns with his political and policy interests. One of his main priorities is building American clout in the Western Hemisphere, where he is leaving an imprint.
He helped forge an oil deal with Venezuela this summer that the Trump administration believes will buoy both the U.S. and Venezuelan economies.
Earlier this month, Rubio met with heads of state in Latin America as he sought to combat illegal immigration and drug trafficking.
The son of Cuban émigrés, he is also driving the administration’s effort to transform Cuba and bring an end to the regime in Havana.
If he can nudge Venezuela and Cuba toward democratic governance, that could be an enviable legacy for a secretary of state who is nursing presidential ambitions.

Rubio’s statement to a Colombian radio station earlier this month that he currently has “no plans” to mount another campaign was not a hard-and-fast denial. Even if it was, it might not matter. When Rubio first ran for president, he made clear he was done with the Senate. And he sounded adamant.

“I have only said like 10000 times I will be a private citizen in January,” he wrote on social media in May 2016, two months after he dropped out of the presidential contest. The following month, he did an about-face, ran for re-election and won.
If Vance enters the race and falters in the Republican primaries, Rubio might jump in the contest, the second person close to Rubio said.

Another possibility would be for Rubio to become Vance’s running mate, something he would be inclined to do if asked, this person said. Trump himself has suggested the two men pair up in 2028, and his opinion counts given his grip on the Republican base.
Trump likes to ask people privately who they think should be the GOP nominee.

“Whoever the Republican nominee is in 2028, Donald Trump will decide,” the White House official said. “Of course, the primary process will run. But the president will have such an outsized influence in it, and I think he does wish they would run together.”
After the midterm elections in November, attention will turn to 2028 and the post-Trump era. Rubio won’t have much time to decide his future.

“If he’s serious about running, he would have to say so reasonably soon,” the White House official said. “Once you’re elected, you never really get rid of that bug. Ultimately, if there’s an opportunity and an opening, you’d be almost fighting your instincts not to do it.”

title: House passes Russia sanctions bill named for Lindsey Graham, sending it to Trump
summary: The legislation, which passed the Senate last month, would target Russia’s energy sector by punishing the largest buyers of its oil and gas to slash revenues Russia uses to attack Ukraine.
story: WASHINGTON — The House voted Wednesday to pass a major bill aimed at imposing sanctions on Russia and Iran, sending it to President Donald Trump for his signature.
The vote was 262-159.

The 61-page legislation, which passed the Senate 86-11 last month, was named the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, in honor of the late senator, who was an outspoken proponent of the cause before his unexpected death in July.

The bill takes aim at Russia’s energy sector by punishing the largest buyers of its oil and gas, allowing the president to impose tariffs on goods from those countries, which may include China and India.
The goal: to slash the revenue streams that fund Russia’s ongoing war on Ukraine, which began in 2022.
Add to Google
Add to Google

“The act’s most consequential new authority is its provision to place tariffs of up to 100 percent on third countries purchasing significant volumes of Russian energy,” according to the nonpartisan Center for Strategic and International Studies. “This replaces the blanket 500 percent tariff in the 2025 version with a more measured instrument, alongside a carve-out for countries taking significant steps to reduce dependence on Russian energy and whose imports amount to less than 15 percent of Russia’s annual natural gas exports.”

The Atlantic Council said the bill would “authorize the Trump administration to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on Chinese imports on national security grounds if China continues purchasing Russian oil. This approach assumes that tariffs will compel China to reduce imports of Russian energy.”
The measure would also target Russian government officials, as well as oligarchs, some family members and Russian financial institutions.
At Trump’s request, the package would also extend sanction authority aimed at slashing funding for Iran’s weapons and energy sectors.
Add to Google
Add to Google
Some top House Democrats criticized the bill, fretting that it would grant broad tariff authorities that Trump could abuse. But in the end, those hesitations weren’t enough to scuttle it.
“I have always been in favor of the Russia sanctions bill,” House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., told reporters Monday. “But we had to build a consensus around it, and I think we have it.”
Daniel Balson of Razom for Ukraine, a U.S. advocacy group supporting Ukraine, called the bill’s passage “momentous.”

“It comes as Russian officials move towards full-scale mobilization and intensify their bombing campaign against Ukraine’s critical energy infrastructure,” he said in a statement. “This bill sends an unmistakable message: for so long as Putin continues to inflict suffering on Ukraine, Congress will continue to impose consequences on Putin.”

title: Saudi Arabia accuses Houthis of attacking Mecca, warns holy city is a ‘red line’
summary: The Iran-backed Yemeni rebels denied targeting the city in their escalating campaign against the key U.S. ally.
story: Saudi Arabia has accused the Iran-backed Houthi rebels of attempting to attack Islam’s holiest city, declaring Mecca a “red line” in the escalating conflict.
The kingdom’s claim drew condemnation from across the Middle East, but no immediate sign of military support as fears grew of a return to all-out war between the key U.S. ally and the Yemeni rebels.

The Houthis swiftly denied targeting Mecca, saying their operations had targeted Saudi oil facilities and military bases, “far removed” from the sacred site of the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad. They accused Saudi Arabia of spreading “fabrications and lies.”

The Houthis’ rapid ground advance in Yemen and aerial attacks on Saudi Arabia have shut down a crucial oil pipeline, threatened energy supplies through a second major shipping route and left the kingdom struggling to respond.

The mounting hostilities have threatened to open a second front in the Iran war, with oil and gas prices rising.  President Donald Trump has so far offered no sign of any U.S. plans to intervene in this new theater.

The United States on Wednesday upgraded its travel advisory to Saudi Arabia to Level 3 amid the escalating conflict, warning Americans to “reconsider travel” to the kingdom and banning government employees from travel near the Yemen border.

Saudi military spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said Wednesday that the country’s air defense forces had intercepted the drone south of Mecca just before 7 p.m. local time Tuesday (12 p.m. ET), according to a statement.

He emphasized that the security of the holy city and of pilgrims was a “red line,” warning there would be no hesitation to take “necessary and deterrent measures” against the Houthis, the statement said.
Mecca is known as the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad, with millions of Muslims from around the world making the pilgrimage to the holy city each year.

“While the Houthis and Saudi Arabia trade barbs over whether the target was Mecca or not,” said Adam Baron, a fellow at New America, a think tank based in Washington, D.C., who follows Yemen and the wider Gulf region, “what is clear is you’re seeing a real demonstration of the Houthis’ continued strategic depth.”
He added: “The fact that they were able to strike this deep in Saudi Arabia is really a signal toward their capacity, if not future intentions.”
The Iran-backed rebels have ramped up attacks on cities across the kingdom after also capturing a key Red Sea port city and island in their bid to gain control of the crucial Bab el Mandeb Strait.

Oil prices have soared over fears that the Houthis could shut down the waterway, which has been a crucial transit route for Saudi Arabian oil exports with the Strait of Hormuz largely closed by Iran since the U.S. and Israel launched their war in late February.
The international benchmark, Brent crude, was at around $108 per barrel early Wednesday. The nationwide average cost of diesel fuel hit another all-time high of $6.31.
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the alleged Mecca attack as a “dastardly and heinous” act.
Sharif, who recently reached a joint defense agreement with Saudi Arabia, did not directly mention the Houthis in his statement, but reiterated Pakistan’s general support for the kingdom.
The U.S. conducted a deadly bombing campaign against the Houthis last year, but has shown little appetite for another.

Trump said over the weekend that the Houthis had called his administration and said they “don’t want to fight with us.” Speaking with reporters during a visit to Dublin on Saturday, he said he also spoke with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and maintained that everything would “work out fine and dandy” in the region.
The Houthis and the opposing coalition backing the internationally supported Yemeni government have been fighting a civil war since 2014, with no clear resolution despite a truce agreed years ago.
The United Nations Security Council met Tuesday in an emergency session to discuss the rising violence in Yemen, the region’s poorest country, with member countries urging de-escalation.
The U.N. warned that the ongoing clashes between Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and Houthi rebels have displaced at least 125,000 people since the start of September.

title: King Charles issues fiery response to Princess Diana’s brother over claims in new book
summary: In a rare rebuke, Buckingham Palace issued a robust statement aimed at King Charles III’s former brother-in-law, Earl Charles Spencer, as he is set to release his bombshell memoir.
story: LONDON — Buckingham Palace has issued a rare and unusually forceful denial after the brother of the late Princess Diana claimed that the then-Prince Charles said his first wife would soon be forgotten in the days after her death.
In a soon-to-be published memoir, Charles Spencer recounts the emotional days in the aftermath of Diana’s 1997 death in a Paris car crash at the age of 36.

One excerpt published Wednesday alleges a heated exchange with Charles, now the British king, over whether Princes William and Harry — then 15 and 12 — should walk behind their mother’s coffin in the funeral procession.

Spencer says he expressed that Diana would not want them to endure such an ordeal, and claims this was met with a “stream of anger” from Charles. The aristocrat writes that Charles “unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death. ‘Rest assured,’ he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough.’”
In response, Buckingham Palace issued a forceful statement denying the claims and suggesting that grief for his older sister may have affected Spencer’s memory.

“While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss,” said the statement, released Wednesday.
Diana’s 1997 funeral procession is etched into modern memory.
Her brother and two young sons were among those who walked solemnly behind her coffin as it passed through central London.
Further excerpts published Thursday continued to provide difficult reading for the palace, reflecting on the breakdown of Diana and Charles’ marriage.
Spencer wrote that his sister “told me that things became very difficult indeed in the marriage early on, and I am sure that both spouses despaired of the other at times.”
“I am not hypocritical enough to judge or criticise anyone else’s marital record. I am merely recording how my sister felt and am not assessing whether she was right or not,” he adds.

Spencer also wrote about his late sister’s struggle with an eating disorder, which Diana spoke about during her lifetime, as well as her wider mental state, criticizing her transfer from a long-serving family doctor to a royal physician.

“It is a sad fact that, in her later years, Diana drove herself more than once to Beachy Head, the highest chalk sea cliff in England, while contemplating ending it all. Her love for her sons stopped her from going further,” he wrote.
Meanwhile, Spencer says that when he spoke to Charles by phone in the hours after Diana’s death, “he sounded giddily elated – like a lottery winner, I remember thinking at the time.”

He wrote: “Looking back now, I suspect the prince’s first reaction must have been to think more of how this event might free him to marry the woman he loved, rather than appreciating the loss of one he did not. It can be hard to feel too much sympathy for an ex-spouse, or those who care for them profoundly, after bitter divorce.”
The palace declined to further comment Thursday.

India McTaggart, a royal correspondent at The Telegraph newspaper, told NBC News of Wednesday’s statement: “Earl Spencer’s book is expected to contain a number of incendiary claims, and perhaps this was the palace trying to get on the front foot and get ahead of some of the allegations we expect to see.”
The royal family mostly avoided commenting when Prince Harry published his autobiography “Spare” in 2023, which also garnered global headlines with claims of bitter family feuds.

Queen Elizabeth II famously issued a brief but forceful statement in 2021 following allegations from Harry and his wife, Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, of racism in the family. “Recollections may vary,” the late queen noted.
“The palace will certainly be bracing for more headlines” as a result of the new memoir, McTaggart said.
Add to Google
Add to Google

“At the same time, we’ll see Harry carrying out public engagements this week, while the king and the prince and princess of Wales continue with theirs. It will be interesting to see how all of that is covered now that they’re all in Britain at the same time.”

Diana was one of the most photographed women in the world after marrying Charles in 1981. Their high-profile marriage ended in 1996 and she died a year later, after being chased by paparazzi with her partner Dodi Fayed. Her death in a Paris tunnel brought the world to a standstill.

At the time of her funeral, the royal family received criticism from the public and the press for appearing to be slow to react to the outpouring of love and grief from the public for a woman posthumously dubbed the “people’s princess.”
Spencer’s book, “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” is due to be published on Tuesday. Britain’s Daily Mail newspaper is publishing excerpts in advance of the publication.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7, to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

The National Alliance for Eating Disorders Helpline provides support, resources and information about treatment options at 1-866-662-1235, Monday through Friday. You can also text “ALLIANCE” to 741741 if you are experiencing a crisis to be contacted by a trained volunteer. More information about eating disorders, including other free and low-cost support options, can be found on the National Eating Disorder Association’s website.

title: Australian athlete apologizes after winning race despite involuntary bowel movement
summary: An Australian athlete apologized Thursday for continuing — and winning — her race in China over the weekend after experiencing an involuntary bowel movement during competition.
story: An Australian athlete apologized Thursday for continuing — and winning — her race in China over the weekend after experiencing an involuntary bowel movement during competition.
Joanna Wietrzyk, a 24-year-old from Melbourne, said she should have pulled off the track during the women’s 16-to-24 Hyrox event in Beijing on Saturday.
The athlete said she hadn’t felt any symptoms before the race that might have warned her about what was to come.
“I want to offer my sincere apology to the people of China, my fellow competitors, the spectators and the HYROX organizers for what happened during the race in Beijing,” Wietrzyk said in statement.

“I felt completely fit and healthy at the start of the race, with no reason to expect any illness. Looking back, I regret the decision to not have stepped off the track. I recognize that I should have made a different choice. I take responsibility for my decision to continue and am deeply sorry for the discomfort and disruption it caused.”

Hyrox is a relatively new indoor sport that combines running and performing high-intensity exercises at various workout stations. It’s not an Olympic sport, but its backers hope it could make the Games in 2032 or 2036.

“I know my actions had an impact beyond myself, and I am genuinely sorry to everyone who was affected,” Wietrzyk said. “I am learning from this experience and will carry those lessons with me, including remembering that there is more to life than racing and knowing when it is right to step away.”
Hyrox co-founder Moritz Fürste apologized for the incident on Sunday and said organizers should have intervened immediately.
Wietrzyk’s time of 1:01:23 would have put her atop her division, but she has asked to “retroactively withdraw” from competition.

“On reflection, I have decided to retroactively withdraw from the race and forfeit the points I earned,” Wietrzyk said. “Thank you to those standing by me, both as an athlete and as a person, during this time, and to everyone who has reached out with kindness and support. It means more to me than I can properly express right now. I will be taking some time to recover, reflect and look after myself and my family away from the noise.”

title: New wild cat species is identified for first time in 100 years, researchers say
summary: Researchers say they’ve identified a new species of wild cat previously unknown to science. The Tilcayo tiger cat is smaller than a typical house cat and lives in the Bolivian cloud forest.
story: For the first time in a century, researchers say they’ve identified a new species of wild cat previously unknown to science.

Leopardus tilcayo — or the tilcayo tiger cat — is slender and spotted, with rounded ears. It is smaller than a typical house cat and lives in the Bolivian Yungas, the cloud forest where the Andes mountains meet the Amazon basin. The species was described for the first time in the journal Current Biology on Thursday.

It’s rare to find a new, relatively large mammal. Unsurprisingly, most newly discovered animal species are small in size, said Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, who co-authored the study and leads a wild cat conservation program called Programa de Investigación de Félidos Bolivia (Bolivian Felid Research and Conservation Program).
“This time, it’s a cat. That’s really novel. And it hasn’t happened in 100 years,” she said. “No one else had named it. No one else had described it.”
The size of the Leopardus tilcayo population is not clear yet.

“We really don’t know how many cats are still in the wild,” said Nogales-Ascarrunz, whose work as a conservationist is funded by National Geographic. “We need science, we need more studies to answer this question, which is actually critical for its conservation.”

title: U.S. accuses Russia of plot to kill a prominent dissident in Washington
summary: The Justice Department unsealed charges against five people it alleged were part of the Kremlin’s “global assassination network” aimed at causing “destruction and mayhem.”
story: The Kremlin orchestrated a murder-for-hire plot against a prominent Russian dissident in Washington this summer, according to the Justice Department, which unsealed charges against five people it alleges were part of a “global assassination network” aimed at causing “destruction and mayhem around the world.”

The five people are still at large, the Justice Department said in the indictment, which was unsealed late Tuesday, describing the wider operation being run by Russian intelligence as “brazen, aggressive, and far-reaching.”
The FBI said it had disrupted the plot, although officials did not detail how.

Since at least 2024, the network is alleged to have paid Americans and foreigners to spy on targets, “carry out targeted killings” and “commit acts of terrorism against civilian and military infrastructure in European countries that are aligned, or perceived to be aligned, with Ukraine,” the Justice Department said.

Asked for a response to the allegations by NBC News, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on a daily briefing call with reporters that “until we have heard or seen any reasonable evidence and arguments based on at least something tangible, we do not consider it necessary to comment on this news.”
Western governments have accused Russia for decades of carrying out attempted and successful killings abroad. Despite substantial evidence, it has always denied the allegations.

The indictment did not name the intended victim in Washington. The Justice Department lists the defendants as Yuri Khrameev, known as “Colonel Yuri,” 63, and his son Kirill Khrameev, 27, both of Russia; Oemis Romagoza Durruthy and Yaidel Delgado Suarez, known as “Viking,” both 35 and Cuban nationals; and Angel Eduardo Castro, 22, of Venezuela.
The indictment describes Durruthy as “an influential member of the Cuban diaspora living in Russia,” where, it says, Suarez and Castro also reside.
All face a charge of conspiracy to finance terrorism. Yuri Khrameev, Suarez and Castro face an additional charge of conspiracy to commit murder for hire.
Yuri Khrameev is alleged to be a former Russian intelligence colonel, while his son is an officer in Russia’s Federal Security Service, or FSB.

Prosecutors allege the network recruited a Venezuelan citizen living in Brooklyn, New York, this summer, promising him between $1,000 and $1,500 to photograph and record two locations associated with the Washington target.

The man carried out the surveillance but declined an offer from Suarez and Castro of $40,000 to “eliminate” or “disappear” the target himself, prosecutors said. The alleged recruiters asked whether he knew somebody who would.
Suarez also offered substantial sums of money to other people in the U.S. to finish the job, the indictment says.

The indictment quotes messages that prosecutors said show the conspirators referred to murder as “construction.” Surveillance instructions included putting the man’s phone into airplane mode and recording while passing the house.
Suarez is alleged to have said that he also had people in Mexico who could carry out the killing but that they were delayed.
Authorities allege a second plot involving a dissident believed to be living in Lithuania whom the network accused of making derogatory statements about Russia.

In that case, a U.S. citizen was promised $200 to photograph the target’s address last year and then was offered around $25,000 to kill him, prosecutors said. When he refused, Yuri Khrameev offered a “simpler job,” prosecutors said — setting fire to a warehouse or attacking an electricity substation.
The purpose, Khrameev is alleged to have said, was to target “all the countries that are helping Ukraine.”
Durruthy, meanwhile, is accused of coordinating logistics for attacks in Prague in June 2024 and Lithuania that September.
Lithuanian authorities publicly named Durruthy as wanted in January in a case involving attempts to burn military equipment intended for Ukraine, according to the Lithuanian broadcaster LRT.

“These defendants allegedly operated as part of a global assassination network that reached into the United States, attempting to recruit U.S. citizens and foreigners to carry out killings at the behest of the Kremlin,” said John A. Eisenberg, the assistant attorney general for national security.
“Actions like these represent a gross violation of our sovereignty and a threat to our national security,” he said.
James C. Barnacle Jr., head of New York’s FBI office, said the agency “disrupted this operation through relentless work and rock-solid partnership.”

title: Hyrox co-founder apologizes after athlete allowed to continue despite defecating on herself
summary: Professional athlete Joanna Wietrzyk was seen on video and in photographs running and using shared fitness equipment with feces running down her legs.
story: The international indoor sports competition Hyrox apologized after an incident in Beijing where a runner was allowed to continue a race after soiling herself during the event.

Professional athlete Joanna Wietrzyk finished and won the competition on Saturday, which consists of running and high-intensity exercises. The athlete was seen on video and in photographs racing and using shared fitness equipment with feces running down her legs.

Competitors alternate between running a kilometer and performing exercises at workout stations, including sled pushes and pulls, burpees, rowing and lunges while carrying sandbags. Wietrzyk holds a world record in the Hyrox women’s solo event.

Hyrox co-founder Moritz Fürste issued a statement Sunday on social media apologizing “to all that were directly or indirectly affected, as well as to everyone who felt like we did not handle the situation like we should have.”
“HYROX made a mistake by not reacting immediately during the race,” he wrote. “In the end it is my job to foresee these potential incidents — and I did not.”
Fürste said Hyrox made changes to its rules and procedures for the event as a result of the incident, but did not elaborate on what those changes were.
“As of this moment, there are new rules and procedures in place to prevent situations like this from happening again,” he said.

In another statement on social media, the company said: “As our sport continues to evolve we are encountering new and increasingly complex situations that challenge us and where additional clarity is needed.” The statement has since been removed.

“We ask our athletes to push themselves to the highest levels. At times, they will go beyond what even we thought was possible,” the brand said. “That courage, resilience and refusal to give in are precisely what makes elite athletes so extraordinary. Our role is to give them the right framework and the right boundaries within which they can compete, perform and express themselves at their very best.”

The brand said it has “clear biocontaminant and medical procedures in place. In this instance, an unforeseen situation arose in which protocols designed for elite competition and mass participation became blurred, creating ambiguity in how they were applied and understood.”

“We recognise that this can understandably lead to frustration, questions and strong views within our community,” the statement said. “Those concerns are legitimate and, as organisers, we must be prepared to hear them, examine what happened and take responsibility for continuing to improve.”
Hyrox did not immediately respond to requests for comment on why the post was taken down or what specific policy changes were made in response to Saturday’s race.
Wietrzyk did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

According to The Guardian, Wietrzyk posted and later deleted an image of herself to her Instagram Story from what appeared to be a hospital bed that read, “Go hard or go home … a win is a win. In all seriousness, thank you for all the support. I’ll be back soon.”

title: U.S. and China face grave AI risks, but mutual distrust stalls cooperation
summary: Foremost among the threats for Beijing is the risk to the ruling Communist Party, which worries the technology could be weaponized against it.
story: BEIJING — The United States and China are both gripped by safety fears as they reckon with their rapid advances in AI, but intensifying competition and deep mutual distrust could derail the kind of cooperation experts say is vital to head off the strategically vital technology’s greatest dangers.

Artificial intelligence is increasingly at the center of the rivalry between Washington and Beijing, and it is expected to be a major topic of discussion at a summit in Washington next week between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

The summit comes as AI leaders and researchers in the U.S. warn that companies should “slow the pace” of AI development, citing recent incidents involving autonomous agents. Trump has dismissed such concerns as a “hoax” while agreeing with executives such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei that the U.S. must maintain AI dominance over China through export controls and other measures.
How exactly could AI cause widespread danger?

China, which tightly regulates AI and largely avoids the existential worries the technology provokes in the U.S., has interpreted calls to slow its development as targeted squarely at its own progress. U.S. companies say the Chinese AI sector is being driven in part by large-scale “illicit distillation” of their most advanced models.
Chinese officials, who say distillation is a conventional practice that U.S. companies also use on Chinese models, in turn accuse America’s AI executives of trying to stave off competition.
Senior Col. Zhu Qichao, a noted voice on Chinese military AI and national security, called for “cooperation” with the U.S. while warning against “vicious competition.”

“Because with the development of emerging technologies, it definitely comes with many possibilities,” said Zhu, the director of the Institute for Defense Technology and Strategic Studies at the People’s Liberation Army National University of Defense Technology.
“On one hand, it benefits humanity, but on the other hand, there are also considerations regarding risks,” he told NBC News on Tuesday at the Xiangshan Forum in Beijing.

AI and the worries around it were a major focus at the annual defense forum, where rooms were packed with scholars, military officials and commentators from the U.S. and other countries, many of which are being pressured to pick sides in the U.S.-China AI race.
Though Trump and Xi agreed at their May summit in Beijing to hold high-level AI talks, no such talks have been publicly confirmed ahead of Xi’s visit next week.
Wu Xinbo, dean of the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai, said China was wary that the talks could be used to further slow its progress.

“On the other hand, I think both sides need to sit down to talk about the risks posed by AI development,” he said at the forum, adding that “it will take a long way before the two sides can really forge some important consensus on this issue.”
For U.S.-China cooperation to work, the U.S. needs to be open to both sides benefiting, said Francesca Giovannini, executive director of the Harvard Belfer Center’s Initiative on Managing the Atom.

“The United States operates on a very specific type of theory. And the theory is, whoever wins the AI race wins everything,” she said in an interview at the forum. “So if this is your zero-sum game idea, you won’t be conceding anything.”

China is unlikely to agree to a slowdown at the behest of U.S. AI companies, said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at the Asia Group, an American strategic advisory firm based in Washington.

“I don’t think what happens in the U.S. really matters to China,” he said Tuesday in a phone interview from Hong Kong. “They want to do AI at their own pace, and to a very large degree a lot of people in the industry, in the government, they have a very proud sense that this is finally the chance for China.”

China, which sees its “open-weight” AI models as a tool for diplomacy, has promoted the technology as a global “public good” that should be managed by the international community. At a summit in India on Sunday, Xi offered the 11-member BRICS group of nations help developing open-source AI and urged them to join China’s global AI governance initiative.
But China is also keenly aware of the risks it faces from its own AI success, with Xi telling a Shanghai conference in July that authorities must “ensure that AI is always under human control.”

The industry must make mandatory filings and submit security assessments to officials, with many of the companies having to submit technical filings to an algorithm registry. The government has also imposed rules requiring watermarking and safety requirements.

Foremost among the risks are potential threats to China’s ruling Communist Party, which worries the technology could be weaponized against it and has imposed ideological controls to ensure products fall in line with socialist values, for example.

“Hostile forces and individuals with ulterior motives misuse generative AI technologies — such as deepfake audio-video, AI-generated graphics and text, and intelligent bot farms — to manufacture political rumors, spread harmful information, and incite confrontation at low cost and on a massive scale,” Chen Yixin, the Chinese minister of state security, said in an article Sunday in the state-backed China Cybersecurity Magazine that called for greater party control and government oversight of AI.

Chen said AI could enable misinformation campaigns and cyberattacks on China’s critical infrastructure and, in an apparent reference to the U.S., warned that countries with “advantages” in AI could restrict other nations’ access to their technologies.

He also warned of espionage and data leaks, days after Anthropic released a report that found Chinese AI labs had secretly routed requests to its Claude models, some of which contained sensitive information from individuals, major companies and state-affiliated actors.

Like the U.S., China increasingly views AI as a national security issue, down to the individual researchers working on it. On Tuesday, China tightened travel curbs on its citizens, barring some whose work has implications for national technology security from leaving the country.

The new rules add to an extensive AI regulatory regime that includes restrictions on AI companions over mental health concerns, mandated labeling of AI-generated content and a requirement that trained models must use data conforming to Chinese values.

Experts say it could take a major crisis for the U.S. and China to finally work together on AI, much like the 1962 Cuban missile crisis pushed the U.S. and the then-Soviet Union to start negotiating on nuclear weapons.

AI has already had profound military implications, including for targeting, and could be integrated into systems supporting the nuclear chain of command, said David Finkelstein, vice president of the Center for Naval Analyses.
“This is scary stuff, and I think that this is an area where the two sides ought to be sitting down and talking to each other,” he said at the forum.
